It marks the second time in recent months t
items.text:
Anthropic worker claims to have solved a Holy Grail of math problems with the help of AI
A mathematician who works for artificial intelligence giant Anthropic claims he has solved a Holy Grail of math problems with the help of the company's AI tool Claude.
It marks the second time in recent months that an AI company or someone linked to one claims to have cracked a famed unsolved math problem.
Levent Alpöge, a member of the company's technical staff, made the announcement Friday by way of a four-page explanation posted on his website. He said that he believes by working with Claude, he has found a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis.
"Claude and I have had a great time together with such breadth in recent months, but this time Claude far outpaced me near the finish line," Alpöge wrote. "No, Claude flew, and danced, and sparkled near that finish line."
Formulated in 1859, the Riemann Hypothesis centers on the distribution of prime numbers — those that are only divisible by one and themselves — as they grow towards infinity.
Alpöge said his discovery came late Sunday night. He messaged Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei to ask about "my ability to announce," as the San Francisco-based company was about to make major news with its stock market debut.
A day after the company's initial public offering — the most valuable in history — Alpöge revealed he'd solved the problem that has proved elusive for more than 150 years. Anthropic did not respond to an email from The Associated Press requesting comment on Alpöge's claim.
Alpöge released his and Claude's proof of the Riemann Hypothesis within 17 million lines of Lean code, a programing language that allows people to program proofs of mathematical theorems. Traditionally the findings buried in that code would be published in a formal paper, said Alex Kontorovich, distinguished professor and department chair of mathematics at Rutgers University.
"Usually when somebody gives you a paper, that's also kind of code for a proof and you have to actually read the paper, follow it yourself, figure out if you believe every single line in that paper. And when you're done, you should have a deep understanding of why something is true," he said.
He said Claude followed that code and said the proof is true.
"Does that mean I understand it? Not yet. But the computer is extraordinarily picky, way pickier than I am and so if you can satisfy the computer, there's a very, very good chance you're going to satisfy me too," he said. "But I have to do the work."
Hours after the announcement, the Riemann Hypothesis remained listed as unsolved on the Clay Mathematics Institute's website. The institute had selected the hypothesis back in 2000 as one of seven Millennium Prize Problems and offered a reward of $1 million for the solution.
The assessment process of whether the problem has actually been solved takes time, explained Martin Bridson, president of the institute.
"This is an announcement of historic significance, which holds the promise of a dramatic transformation in the perception of what is possible in the struggle to extend the human understanding of mathematics," he said in a statement. "But the journey from today's announcement to a place of real understanding will be long and difficult."
Alpöge said he is "presenting the world with a complete argument before having mastered a massive neighbourhood around its mathematics." He said more than 250,000 pages came out of his work with AI.
In September, OpenAI said its technology was key in a similar breakthrough with Navier-Stokes, an equation that governs the flow of fluids.
"Navier-Stokes fell and now the Riemann Hypothesis," said Kontorovich. "There's some kind of out-of-body experience where I'm looking at myself saying, 'Yes, the Riemann Hypothesis has been solved,' and kind of trying to comprehend what the hell these words are coming out of my mouth."
Anthropic made a blockbuster Wall Street debut this week, through which it raised a record-breaking $81 billion at a $1.5 trillion valuation.
Amodei has projected an optimistic vision for AI's future in which the technology leads to significant advancements in math and science research while simultaneously warning about the potential risks AI poses.

items.text:
Israeli attacks on Gaza kill at least four Palestinians
Three Palestinians were killed in an Israeli drone attack while a Palestinian man was killed by gunfire in Jabalia.
Israeli attacks in Gaza have killed at least four Palestinians in violation of last year’s “ceasefire”, as winter flooding deepens the humanitarian crisis in the enclave.
At least three people were killed when the car they were travelling in was struck by an Israeli drone on Saturday in the Tel al-Hawa neighbourhood of Gaza City. Separately, a Palestinian man was killed by Israeli gunfire in the Halawa displacement camp, east of northern Gaza’s Jabalia refugee camp.
Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza has continued despite a so-called “ceasefire”, which came into force last October.
The ongoing attacks on the enclave coincide with a surge in pogroms carried out by Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank.
Late on Friday, Hamza Masoud Salim Abdo, 42, was shot dead by security guards from an illegal Israeli settlement near the village of Dura al-Qar, north of Ramallah.
The Palestinian Health Ministry said his body was being withheld by Israeli authorities. Another Palestinian man was detained during the incident.
Reporting from Ramallah in the West Bank, Al Jazeera’s Nour Odeh said settlers have been carrying out attacks with “impunity”.
“Less than 3 percent of Israeli attacks that are investigated lead to a partial or full conviction by Israeli authorities. Also, the number of settler attacks reported to Israeli authorities is very, very low because Palestinians are often detained, questioned or harassed for filing reports against violent settlers,” Odeh reported.
The violence inflicted on Palestinians in the West Bank has been condemned by Israeli allies, including the United Kingdom. Critics say Western leaders have not supported their rhetoric with sufficient action.
Earlier this month, an Al Jazeera investigation found that the UK had awarded $14.4m in new public contracts to firms with links to illegal Israeli settlements in the West Bank, despite recently announcing a ban on importing goods from such settlements.
The British government has also sanctioned companies involved in settlement expansion.
Winter weather has compounded the humanitarian crisis in Gaza, with the World Food Programme (WFP) warning earlier this week that Palestinians have been forced to burn rubbish to cook their food.
“Now even the rubbish is wet,” warned Shaun Hughes, WFP’s country director for Palestine.
The International Organization for Migration (IOM) has said that more than 100,000 tents in Egypt cannot be delivered to Gaza due to strict conditions imposed by Israel.
“Usually anything under 38 millimetres is okay; anything above, it’s usually deemed as not acceptable,” Hughes explained.
“It is not a statement of dual use; it is just that this tent at this time is not allowed to enter Gaza … We don’t get the specifics,” said Karl Baker, head of the IOM’s Gaza programme.
Gaza’s Health Ministry reported on Saturday that 1,671 people had been killed since the “ceasefire” came into effect last October.
Meanwhile, 74,736 Palestinians have been killed since Israel launched its genocidal war on Gaza three years ago.

items.title: Kenya targets paediatric HIV treatment gaps in World AIDS Day campaign
items.summary:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 21– Children, adolescents and young people account for 55 per cent of new HIV infections in Kenya, exposing a widening gap in the country’s fight against AIDS despite a significant decline in overall infections.
The latest figures show that Kenya recorded 13,936 new HIV infection
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 21– Children, adolescents and young people account for 55 per cent of new HIV infections in Kenya, exposing a widening gap in the country’s fight against AIDS despite a significant decline in overall infections.
The latest figures show that Kenya recorded 13,936 new HIV infections in 2025, a 56.5 per cent reduction from 32,027 in 2021.
However, children aged 0 to 14 accounted for 3,396 of the infections, highlighting the challenges facing efforts to protect younger populations.
The figures have prompted health authorities to place children and young people at the centre of this year’s World AIDS Day commemorations under the theme, “Protect, Prevent, Empower: Ending AIDS Among Children, Adolescents and Young People.”
The National Syndemic Diseases Control Council (NSDCC), the National AIDS and STI Control Programme (NASCOP), county governments and civil society partners unveiled the programme on Friday, with activities set to begin with a national half marathon at Nyayo National Stadium on November 29 before spreading to all 47 counties on December 1.
The treatment gap among children remains particularly concerning, with Kenya’s HIV treatment cascade for those aged 0 to 14 standing at 79:60:52, compared with the national average of 93:91:87 across the three targets of diagnosis, treatment and viral suppression.
According to the Kenya HIV Estimates 2026, approximately 14,559 of the 69,330 children living with HIV have not been diagnosed, while another 21,908 have been diagnosed but are not receiving treatment.
Nearly half of children receiving treatment are also yet to achieve viral suppression, leaving them at risk of HIV-related complications.
Children account for 4.7 per cent of people living with HIV in the country but represent 11.5 per cent of AIDS-related deaths. Their fatality rate stands at 32.1 per 1,000, compared with 12.2 among adults.
The figures point to persistent challenges in preventing mother-to-child transmission and ensuring children diagnosed with HIV are promptly linked to treatment and retained in care.
Vertical transmission stood at 8.04 per cent in 2025, above the global elimination target of less than five per cent.
Douglas O. Bosire, Chief Executive Officer of NSDCC, said the government was shifting its attention towards the populations most affected by the remaining gaps in the HIV response.
“The 56 per cent fall in new infections since 2021 is a hard-won gain, but it will not hold if we lose our children. The Kenya AIDS Strategic Framework is being executed with children, adolescents and young people at the centre, and with the counties as co-owners of the response,” he said.
Bosire said county activities on December 1 would include public accountability forums where county leaders would be required to report on progress against targets for paediatric HIV diagnosis, treatment and care.
Dr Andrew Mulwa, Head of NASCOP, said the programme was prioritising the prevention of mother-to-child transmission, early infant diagnosis and improved retention of mothers living with HIV on treatment.
“We cannot accept a vertical transmission rate above 5 per cent, and we will not. We are scaling early infant diagnosis, strengthening retention for mothers on treatment and rolling out long-acting prevention, including the twice-yearly injectable PrEP now moving through 15 priority counties,” he said.
The programme will also strengthen sexually transmitted infection surveillance alongside HIV testing, particularly among young people.
The focus on children comes amid concerns over disruptions to HIV services and uncertainty surrounding external financing, which officials and civil society organisations say could undermine progress.
The National Empowerment Network of People Living with HIV/AIDS in Kenya (NEPHAK) raised concerns last year that some members were being charged between Sh500 and Sh2,000 for HIV tests that had previously been provided free of charge, pending clarification of coverage under the Social Health Authority.
Between April and June this year, some patients also received one-to-two-week supplies of antiretroviral drugs instead of the standard three-month refills.
Dr Samuel Kinyanjui, Country Director of AIDS Healthcare Foundation (AHF) Kenya, said children living with HIV could lead healthy lives if they received timely diagnosis and uninterrupted treatment.
“A child born with HIV in Kenya today has every reason to live a full life. Whether she does is now a question of logistics and attention, not of science,” he said.
Alongside the national World AIDS Day programme, the Voices of Impact Awards Committee and AHF Kenya launched the second edition of the #VoicesOfImpact HIV and STIs Media Awards to encourage sustained reporting on HIV-related issues.
The awards, launched in 2025, recognise journalism, advocacy and digital storytelling that challenge stigma, promote dignity and support efforts to end AIDS as a public health threat by 2030.
Entries opened on Friday, with the awards ceremony scheduled for June 18, 2027. The Kenya Editors’ Guild and Media Council of Kenya are supporting the initiative.
Victor Bwire, Director of Media Training and Development at the Media Council of Kenya, said responsible reporting was important in addressing stigma and ensuring the experiences of people living with HIV were represented with dignity.
“Accurate, stigma-free reporting is not a favour to the response. It is a professional obligation. The Council will support these awards because they reward the journalism our Code of Conduct already asks for: person-first language, informed consent, protection of children and adolescents, and verification against official sources,” he said.

items.title: Pakistan drop Rizwan and Masood, but back Babar and Agha in overhaul
items.summary:
Pakistan drop Rizwan and Masood, but back Babar and Agha in overhaul
Former captains Mohammad Rizwan and Shan Masood lose Pakistan central contracts, but Babar Azam and Salman Agha backed.
Pakistan’s Cricket Board has announced that it will drop former captains Mohammad Rizwan and Shan Masood in a m
items.text:
Pakistan drop Rizwan and Masood, but back Babar and Agha in overhaul
Former captains Mohammad Rizwan and Shan Masood lose Pakistan central contracts, but Babar Azam and Salman Agha backed.
Pakistan’s Cricket Board has announced that it will drop former captains Mohammad Rizwan and Shan Masood in a major overhaul of its central contract list.
Saturday’s announcement, which expands the pool of contracted players to 38 from 30, comes a day after Pakistan won the second Test against Sri Lanka in Rawalpindi, marking a first series win in two years.
“We are testing new players and these contracts are devised to let players focus on their specific format,” Pakistan selector Aaqib Javed told the media.
The board overhauled the Test squad after the second Test in its disastrous 3-0 defeat against England, sending seven players home and sacking head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed.
White-ball head coach Mike Hesson was given the Test team in a bid to lift the country, which is currently ninth and last in the 2025-27 World Test Championship cycle.
Besides Rizwan and Masood, white-ball specialist Saim Ayub, spinner Noman Ali and pace bowler Hasan Ali are among the 12 players who have been removed from contracts.
Test skipper Babar Azam and recently sacked Twenty20 International (T20I) skipper Salman Agha are in the top category of the 38-player list.
“The ‘AB’ category is for Test and ODIs, ‘A’ for Test-only, ‘BC’ for ODI and T20I players; ‘C’ for T20I specialists; ‘D’ for development players,” said Javed.
The new contracts run from July 2026 to June 2027. Players had been without central contracts since the expiry of the previous cycle in June.
The PCB had said at that time that only male cricketers who had played at least four tests, six one-day internationals or six Twenty20s in the previous 12 months would be eligible for central contracts.
Under the new system, contracts are split into five specialised categories: tests and ODIs, Test specialists, ODIs and T20Is, T20I specialists, and emerging players in the developmental pathway.
The new contracts run through June 30, 2027. Players had been without central contracts since the expiry of the previous cycle in June.

Those teams: Enzo Maresca makes three changes to the City team that started against Nottingham Forest last time out, with Nico O’Reilly, Ayyoub Bouaddi and Phil Foden coming into his side. Josko Gvardiol, Enzo Fernandez and Rayan Cherki drop to the bench. Abdukodir Khusanov and Marc Guehi have both been selected despite missing out on international duty with Uzbekistan and England resepectively through injury.
There are also three changes to the Fulham side that lined up against Newcastle before the international break. Kenny Tete, Ryan Sessegnon and Rodrigo Muniz have been selected today, with Timothy Castagne, Antonee Robinson and Gonzalo Garcia making way.
Manchester City v Fulham line-ups
Manchester City: Donnarumma, Khusanov, Dias, Guehi, O’Reilly, Anderson, Bouaddi, Ndiaye, Foden, Doku, Haaland
Subs: Rulli, Kovacic, Cherki, Fernandez, Reis, Gvardiol, Allan, Samba, Lewis
Fulham: Leno, Tete, Bassey, Affengruber, Sessegnon, Charles, Berge, Iwobi, King, Bobb, Muniz.
Subs: Kaiser, Cuenca, García, Palacios, Cairney, Larsson, Angel, Castagne, Robinson.
Early team news
Manchester City winger Antoine Semenyo remains sidelined with the knee injury he suffered against Ipswich in October, while defenders Marc Guehi and Abdukodir Khushanov have been rated doubtful for today’s game.
Speaking at his press conference yesterday, Fulham head coach Alvaro Arbeloa confirmed that reserve goalkeeper Benjamin Lecomte will be out for the season after rupturing his achillles tendon in a practice match played against West Ham behind closed doors during the international break.
Midfielder Tom Cairney is struggling with a knee injury but could feature in today’s squad, while Emile Smith-Rowe is unlikely to be in the matchday squad as he has a hip injury.
Premier League: Manchester City v Fulham
Following the second international break of the season, the Premier League resumes at the Etihad Stadium, with Manchester City hoping to halt a run of three consecutive defeats in the top flight. The most recent came against Nottingham Forest at the City Ground, where Liam Delap scored two quite extraordinary goals against the club where he learnt his trade.
Fulham are unbeaten in four matches and came from behind to draw with Newcastle at Craven Cottage last time out. Rather astonishingly, they haven’t beaten Manchester City since 2009 and have lost 20 consecutive games against today’s hosts in an extraordinary run of defeats against the same opponents dating back to 2012. Kick-off at the Etihad Stadium is at 12.30pm (GMT) but we’ll have team news and buildup in the meantime.

items.title: Government to open sections of Rironi-Mau Summit highway ahead of Christmas
items.summary:
NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 21 – The Government is accelerating construction of the Rironi–Mau Summit Highway, with completed sections expected to be opened to motorists before Christmas to ease congestion along the busy Nairobi–Nakuru route.
The Ministry of Roads and Transport said the move would allow moto
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 21 – The Government is accelerating construction of the Rironi–Mau Summit Highway, with completed sections expected to be opened to motorists before Christmas to ease congestion along the busy Nairobi–Nakuru route.
The Ministry of Roads and Transport said the move would allow motorists travelling upcountry during the festive season to use sections of the expanded highway as contractors continue working on the remaining portions.
“The Government is fast-tracking works on the Rironi–Mau Summit Highway, with sections set to be opened to motorists ahead of the Christmas festivities to ease traffic congestion, enhance mobility and facilitate smoother journeys,” the Ministry said in a statement on Saturday.
The planned opening comes as thousands of Kenyans prepare to travel from Nairobi to the Rift Valley, Western Kenya and neighbouring regions for the December holidays, a period when the Nairobi–Nakuru highway traditionally experiences heavy traffic.
Roads and Transport Cabinet Secretary Davis Chirchir has previously indicated that the Rironi–Naivasha section, measuring about 60 kilometres, would be accessible to motorists by Christmas 2026.
During an inspection of the works in November, Chirchir said sections that had received the initial layer of tarmac would be temporarily opened to traffic before contractors returned to apply the final asphalt layer.
“But before we do that, we’ll be opening this for traffic for a while in the coming weeks before we do the final layer,” he said.
The first layer of Dense Bituminous Macadam (DBM) has already been laid at Lari, marking a key milestone in the construction of the highway.
Chirchir said the Government had deployed additional equipment to accelerate the works, including 10 asphalt paving machines, with five operating from the Rironi side and another five from Naivasha.
He said the additional machinery would help contractors increase the pace of tarmacking, with the aim of covering about one kilometre daily on the targeted sections.
The project had initially been expected to meet an October 30 deadline for the Rironi–Naivasha stretch, but the timeline was pushed to December after construction delays.
Chirchir attributed some of the setbacks to difficulties in securing adequate supplies of bitumen, a key material used in road construction. He said geopolitical developments and supply chain disruptions had affected availability and slowed progress.
The Government has also urged motorists to exercise caution when using sections that remain under construction, follow instructions from traffic marshals and observe road safety regulations.
The Kenya National Highways Authority (KeNHA) has specifically advised drivers to ensure their vehicles are roadworthy and pay attention to signage and construction activity along the corridor.
The wider Rironi–Mau Summit project is expected to improve transport links between Nairobi, the Rift Valley and western Kenya, while supporting the movement of passengers and goods along the Northern Corridor.
President William Ruto officially launched the project at Manguo, near Rironi, in November 2025. Its implementation forms part of efforts to expand the major transport artery and address persistent congestion on the route.
Although the opening of completed sections is expected to provide some relief during the Christmas travel rush, construction will continue on unfinished sections and associated infrastructure, including works at the Naivasha Junction interchange

items.summary:
Harry Kane: England and Bayern Munich striker vows to be back for ‘business end of season’ after ankle surgery
Harry Kane was withdrawn after 20 minutes of Bayern's Bundesliga game against Cologne; the injury comes days after the England captain became his country's most-capped player; Kane won the
items.text:
Harry Kane: England and Bayern Munich striker vows to be back for ‘business end of season’ after ankle surgery
Harry Kane was withdrawn after 20 minutes of Bayern's Bundesliga game against Cologne; the injury comes days after the England captain became his country's most-capped player; Kane won the Ballon d'Or earlier this month; Michael Olise also taken off injured in 1-1 draw
Saturday 21 November 2026 11:26, UK
Harry Kane is targeting the "business end of the season" after undergoing surgery on a torn ligament in his left ankle.
Bayern Munich said the operation on the injury, sustained in Friday's 1-1 draw with Cologne, was a success but the 33-year-old is expected to be out for months as a result.
Kane wrote on social media: "The highs and lows of life! Obviously very disappointed to get this injury but as always it's an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going into 2027.
- How Bayern Munich fell in love with Harry Kane
- Kane becomes first Englishman to win Ballon d'Or for 25 years
- 'A cinderella story': Kane's journey from EFL loans to Ballon d'Or
"I'll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season!
"Tough times don't last, tough people do" - my guy @edelman11 (Julian Edelman, three-time Super Bowl winner with the New England Patriots) told me this one!
"Thank you for all the messages! Alles gut."
Kane - who became England's most-capped player last week - sustained the injury when he was scythed down in the area by Cologne defender Joel Schmied, who reached Michael Olise's low cross first but clattered into the Ballon d'Or winner's left leg in his follow-through at the back post.
The England captain writhed in pain and, although he gingerly got back to his feet and initially soldiered on, it was clear he could not continue and he hobbled off the field alongside two physios after treatment.
Kane had a quick exchange with Vincent Kompany, who was back in the Bayern hot-seat for the first time in six matches after being diagnosed with meningeal irritation last month, before heading down the tunnel.
After the match Bayern confirmed Kane had torn the syndesmotic ligament and "will therefore be sidelined for the next few months".
Kane earlier this month signed a new deal with the Bundesliga giants until June 2029 - reportedly worth in excess of £400,000 a week, making him the highest-paid player in Europe before bonuses.
Since arriving from Tottenham three years ago, Kane has bagged a scarcely believable 156 goals in 163 appearances in all competitions, helping Bayern win a league and cup double last season.
He went into the international break having a drawn a blank in his four previous matches for Bayern but he scored twice for England, including from the spot in their 3-2 Nations League win over Spain.
But after being forced off after 20 minutes at the Allianz Arena, replaced by Tom Bischof, Kane could now be facing a battle to be fully fit for England's two-legged quarter-final against Norway in March.
How many games will Kane miss?
A three-month period on the sidelines would rule Kane out for 11 Bundesliga games, the DFB-Pokal round of 16 tie against Hertha Berlin, as well as all four of Bayern's remaining Champions League league phase matches.
Providing his recovery goes to plan, that would give the striker just over a month to prepare for England's Nations League quarter-final.
The Three Lions face Norway in Oslo in the first leg on March 27, before the return leg at Wembley on March 30.
'This will concern Tuchel'
Henry Winter speaking on Back Pages Tonight:
"I've covered Harry Kane's career for so many years and there was a period where he had almost a chronic problem with his ankles.
"It's three months and, most immediately, it's Bayern Munich's concern. But England have the home and away Nations League quarter-finals against Norway in late March.
"The timeline would suggest he'll be back in that time, but thoughts with Thomas Tuchel tonight because he'll be absolutely concerned about this.
"He's such an important player. England's No 9. There's a bit of a gap behind him if you're looking for No 9s. I know Jude Bellingham can play there and that's probably the long-term plan. But this is hugely alarming."

items.title: Quality indigenous tree seed key to climate-resilient restoration in Eastern Africa
items.summary:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 21 – The success of landscape restoration efforts in Eastern Africa will increasingly depend on the quality and origin of tree seeds, as climate change alters rainfall patterns and threatens the survival of newly planted trees.
Experts have warned that planting trees without cons
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 21 – The success of landscape restoration efforts in Eastern Africa will increasingly depend on the quality and origin of tree seeds, as climate change alters rainfall patterns and threatens the survival of newly planted trees.
Experts have warned that planting trees without considering their suitability to future climatic conditions risks undermining restoration investments, calling for greater investment in quality indigenous seeds and stronger community participation in tree seed production.
The issue featured prominently at the first Eastern Africa Indigenous Seed Conference, held from November 17–20 at the Catholic University of Eastern Africa in Nairobi, which brought together farmers, researchers, policymakers, seed custodians and development partners to strengthen farmer-managed seed systems across the region.
Sammy Carsan, Agroforestry Specialist at Landscape Alliance, said selecting appropriate seed sources was critical to ensuring trees planted today could survive changing environmental conditions in the years ahead.
“The tree you plant today has to survive the climate of future years. And that depends on the seed you choose today,” he said.
Carsan said restoration practitioners needed to consider tree species characteristics, local environmental conditions and projected climate changes when selecting seeds, warning that unsuitable choices could leave restored landscapes vulnerable as temperatures rise and rainfall becomes increasingly unpredictable.
Roeland Kindt, Senior Ecologist at Landscape Alliance, highlighted the role of scientific research and digital tools in helping practitioners identify suitable indigenous tree species and seed sources for different locations.
He showcased the organisation’s Global Useful Native Trees (GlobUNT) database, which provides information on useful tree species and supports evidence-based decisions on species selection and seed sourcing.
“The underlying principle is simple. We need to have the right tree in the right place, using the right seed source. And digital tools are helping us to do that,” he said.
The tools can help restoration practitioners assess the suitability of native species under different climatic conditions and identify appropriate seed sources for specific planting locations, an important consideration given the ecological diversity of Eastern Africa.
Beyond environmental restoration, experts and community initiatives highlighted the economic opportunities presented by indigenous tree seed production, particularly for farmers and rural communities.
Indigenous tree seed collection, production and nursery enterprises can provide income and employment opportunities while supplying planting materials for conservation and restoration programmes.
Paul Mwanza, Chief Executive Officer and co-founder of Palma Mukuyuni Tree Nursery, said indigenous trees offered communities an opportunity to develop viable businesses while contributing to environmental conservation.
“You can generate income and create a business with indigenous trees, so it is something we should embrace,” he said.
The discussions underscored the importance of involving farmers and local communities across the seed value chain, from collecting and conserving indigenous seeds to producing seedlings and supplying restoration initiatives.
Such participation could strengthen local seed supply systems, create alternative livelihoods and ensure communities benefit from growing investments in landscape restoration.
The conference also highlighted the need to connect scientific research with traditional knowledge and practical conservation efforts, with experts emphasising that successful restoration requires collaboration between researchers, farmers, policymakers and seed enterprises.

items.title: Russian missiles hit Poland: What happened, and could NATO respond?
items.summary:
Russian missiles hit Poland: What happened, and could NATO respond?
Warsaw accuses Moscow of intentional provocation, but the bar for triggering NATO’s collective defence clause remains high.
Security cameras captured the moment a suspected Russian missile struck Polish territory during an attack on
items.text:
Russian missiles hit Poland: What happened, and could NATO respond?
Warsaw accuses Moscow of intentional provocation, but the bar for triggering NATO’s collective defence clause remains high.
Security cameras captured the moment a suspected Russian missile struck Polish territory during an attack on Ukraine on Friday. Poland’s government says it may have been hit by two missiles and a jet-powered drone.
The incident, which took place as European troops held military drills in the country and as the United States pushes to revive talks on ending the war in Ukraine, have raised questions about whether the strike was deliberate.
So what happened, and does this mean Russia has struck Poland, a NATO member?
What happened in Poland?
Poland’s Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz told a news conference in Warsaw that two missiles and a jet-powered drone fell on Polish territory during Russia’s overnight attack on November 20. The missiles came down at Nowy Lipowiec and Rudnik nad Sanem, while the jet-powered drone fell at Molodycz, all in the country’s southeast.
One missile is believed to have crashed about 35km (22 miles) from where European troops’ military exercises were taking place. A Kh-101 cruise missile went down about 50km (31 miles) from the Ukrainian border, and what officials believe was a jet-powered drone hit about 30km (20 miles) from the border. No immediate injuries or damage were reported.
That night, Russia launched one of its heaviest bombardments of Ukraine. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia fired more than 400 drones and at least 110 missiles, including 27 ballistic missiles, some with cluster warheads. At least eight civilians were killed and more than two dozen were wounded.
Why did a Russian missile enter Polish airspace?
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said it appeared “we are dealing with an intentional provocation” by Russia. He said the incident was likely timed to coincide with the European military exercises in Poland. The unprecedented two-week exercise began on November 9 in southeastern Poland and is preparing forces for a possible post-war mission in Ukraine to help stabilise the country and rebuild its military.
Scott Lucas, professor of international politics at the Clinton Institute, University College Dublin, told Al Jazeera that the incident “fits into a pattern going back for months” of Russia “testing how far they can go”.
“A few months ago, it was flying the drones into airspace, and indeed a couple of times they flew fighter jets across the border into the Baltic states,” he said. “You just test how NATO responds.”
This time, he said, Moscow had “gone a bit further”. “You lob a couple of missiles across and a drone” near where 11 countries are holding exercises.
The Polish Air Force had launched preventive air patrols on September 17 aimed at securing the eastern part of Polish airspace following repeated incursions in the previous weeks.
Harry Nedelcu, partner and senior director for geopolitics at Rasmussen Global, said the testing has not been limited to Poland.
“During the war, there’s been repeated instances of Russia testing NATO allies – Poland, Romania and also non-NATO Moldova as well, which is experiencing – especially over the last few months – increasing numbers of drones and missiles flying over its territory and airspace,” he told Al Jazeera.
He linked the incursions to one of Moscow’s core war aims. “One of the key goals in Ukraine that Russia has had in the full-scale invasion, that has lasted almost five years now, has been to prevent Ukraine from being a part of NATO,” he said. “So their goal clearly is to undermine NATO, to do everything possible to undermine it.
“What Russia is doing with these missiles, drones, that sometimes find their way into NATO territory, tests NATO just under the radar of Article 5 to see how far can they push things. How far can they take hybrid warfare?”
Under Article 5, each member of the NATO alliance understands that if one of them is the “victim of an armed attack, each and every other member of the alliance will consider this act of violence as an armed attack against all members”.
Why has this happened now?
At a meeting on Thursday with European leaders in Germany’s capital, Berlin, US President Donald Trump’s envoy and son-in-law Jared Kushner said he believes Russia would be “comfortable” with NATO-like security guarantees for post-war Ukraine.
Kushner and fellow special envoy Steve Witkoff have been holding talks with Ukraine and Russia in recent days, in a push for peace which has been viewed as sidelining Ukraine’s European allies.
Following the Berlin meeting, French President Emmanuel Macron said Ukraine’s membership of NATO should be considered again, prompting Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergey Ryabkov to push back.
Ryabkov said any form of “quasi membership” for Kyiv of the Western military alliance was totally unacceptable for Moscow, Russian state media reported.

“The Russians cannot be seen to go through talks and completely exclude Europe,” he said. He described the Kremlin’s push for a “Europe-wide security architecture” as a way to avoid discussing a ceasefire or security guarantees for Ukraine.
“Rather than having a strong Europe at the talks, they want to try to divide Europe, they want to try to unsettle Europe, they want to try to scare Europe,” he said.
He also pointed to Ukraine’s recent strikes on the Kerch Bridge, which links occupied Crimea to Russia. He said these were seen as “a very serious attack on Russian capabilities” with “severe political, military and economic consequences”.
The latest Russian bombardment follows President Vladimir Putin’s pledge to retaliate against those strikes.

items.text:
A bullet-peppered mural of the Haitian striker Emmanuel Sanon covers the facade of Port-au-Prince’s main football ground. But more than two years have passed since any sports stars graced the pitch.
In 2024, as the surrounding city was almost entirely captured by heavily armed gangs, Sylvio Cator stadium – where football greats including Brazil’s Ronaldo and Roberto Carlos once played – also fell under criminal control, its dilapidated red and blue stands used as an outpost by fighters working for a gang boss called Izo. Haiti’s national team, the Grenadiers, found itself homeless and was forced to play its World Cup qualifying games abroad.
That changed last week, as Haitian police and troops from El Salvador reconquered the stadium. Nayib Bukele, El Salvador’s authoritarian president, called the development a step towards delivering Haiti from a criminal insurrection that has displaced more than 1.5 million people and killed thousands.
“We now have the upper hand on the ground,” claimed Bukele, who has sent more than 2,000 soldiers to Haiti since mid-October.
Outside the Sylvio Cator stadium, named after an acclaimed Haitian athlete who won a silver medal at the 1928 Olympics, there were joyous scenes as citizens celebrated a foreign politician they hope will prove an unlikely saviour.
“There’s a wind of hope blowing through our country and, thanks to God, we will get through this. Long live Bukele!” said a 55-year-old decorator who asked to be named as Bòs Baton.
Stood by Sanon’s battle-scarred fresco, Baton recalled being driven from an area called Poste-Marchand after criminals set his home ablaze during an armed uprising that started in February 2024. “Today, we are happy because there are places we couldn’t go to before that are accessible – and it’s thanks to Bukele’s intervention that we can be here today,” Baton said.
Identical sentiments have been voiced on the streets of El Salvador’s capital, San Salvador, in recent years as a result of Bukele’s controversial anti-gang crusade, which has freed millions from gang rule – albeit at a high price.
Since that crackdown began in early 2022, more than 90,000 Salvadorans have been jailed as part of a mass incarceration campaign that has slashed murder rates but also fuelled fears that El Salvador’s democracy has died.
Bukele’s domestic clampdown has made the millennial strongman a darling for rightwing politicians and voters across Latin America and the Caribbean, who hold his actions up as proof that, with an iron fist and a malleable approach to human rights, rampant criminality can be tamed.
Now, as Bukele seeks to extend his seven-year presidency in an election in February, he is hoping to burnish his gang-busting credentials overseas.
“It’s an operation that projects force, that projects Bukele’s image as the saviour … and positions El Salvador as a key reference in the region for [how] … to deal with gangs and security,” said Tiziano Breda, a Latin America regional expert from the Armed Conflict Location and Event Data project.
The extent of Bukele’s ambitions in Haiti is unclear. The operation’s trigger was the 18 October abduction of four Salvadoran aviation technicians who worked for a UN-backed security force. On Monday, Bukele’s vice-president, Félix Ulloa, announced Salvadoran troops would withdraw as soon as the four men were rescued, “because this is not an occupying force – we are not there to stay”.
But Ulloa also said his government was responding altruistically “to a cry for help from the Haitian people and government”, suggesting its mission could be extended.
Bukele has also hinted his plans go beyond short-lived ground operations to recover his citizens, or their remains. “We will triumph. God will give us victory,” the politician vowed this week.
Many Haitians hope his combatants will stay and have been thrilled by cinematic social media clips posted by Bukele showing helicopter strikes on a gang compound and the mansion of a gangster nicknamed Taliban.
Banners and billboards around Port-au-Prince celebrate Bukele as a 21st-century liberator and feature slogans such as “The bandits won’t get a wink of sleep!” and “We’re tired! Give us Bukele!”
Standing outside the liberated football ground, bricklayer Venel Saindor recalled how criminals torched his home in Carrefour-Feuilles three years ago. “It’s impossible to enter my neighbourhood because the thieves are still there. They shoot at us,” the 56-year-old explained, lifting his shirt to reveal a bullet scar above his right nipple.
“We need Bukele to help us return to our homes,” added Saindor, as a Salvadoran soldier with a belt-fed heavy machine gun kept watch from the stadium’s terraces.
Monique Clesca, a writer and activist, echoed the bricklayer’s enthusiasm. “Haitians are elated … [and] I feel elated also … It is a moment of hope,” she said on Tuesday, as thousands of demonstrators poured on to the streets to champion Bukele, chanting: “Viv Bukele!” and “Bukele is not playing games!”
As a sea of protesters swept towards the prime minister’s offices, people from all walks of life spoke of how armed groups had destroyed their lives and their collective hope that Bukele may provide a solution.
“I used to drive an old bus. The bandits burned it. They burned my house down too,” said Wilné Persona, a 50-year-old driver, adding: “Bukele is the one we are waiting for … because we can no longer bear the situation.”
A food vendor called Claudy Mayas urged “Papa Bukele” to stand his ground. “Bukele, I bless you, your wife and your children,” said Mayas, 51. “The Haitian people are with you, just as you are with us.”
Clesca attributed the palpable excitement to the widespread perception that Bukele’s “decisive” action had exposed the incompetence, inefficiency and indifference of Haitian and foreign leaders. “Basically, what Bukele has done is show that leadership is about resolving a problem for your population,” she said, praising how the stadium and other areas were

items.text:
The FBI is investigating an apparent breach of its criminal information database, US media report citing two people briefed on the issue.
The National Crime Information Center (NCIC) database is used by federal and local law enforcement to share information on warrants and background checks. The BBC has contacted the FBI for comment.
This comes after string of tech outages which hit banking, air traffic control and other sectors in the US last week. Officials have said they were not caused by cyberattacks – but the blackouts have sparked scrutiny from lawmakers.
White House National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross was fired this week, with US President Donald Trump saying he was not good enough.
It would not be the first time hackers have targeted the FBI, the domestic intelligence and security service of the US.
In September, the FBI said it was investigating an apparent breach by a cyber-crime group ShinyHunters, which claimed it had stolen sensitive information on all bureau staff – around 38,000 people.
After that hack, one former FBI agent told the BBC he feared for the safety of current employees, whose personal information could soon become available online to criminals and hostile nation-state hackers.
In a separate development, NBC reported an apparent cyberattack against the US Department of Agriculture (USDA) .

items.title: 'Accept cookies'? Russia collects data from swaths of unknowing Swedes
items.summary:
'Accept cookies'? Russia collects data from swaths of unknowing Swedes
A Russian tech firm backed by an oligarch close to President Vladimir Putin has secretly been collecting data from hundreds of thousands – possibly millions – of Swedes, a newspaper investigation found. The revelation has rattled
items.text:
'Accept cookies'? Russia collects data from swaths of unknowing Swedes
A Russian tech firm backed by an oligarch close to President Vladimir Putin has secretly been collecting data from hundreds of thousands – possibly millions – of Swedes, a newspaper investigation found. The revelation has rattled the Nordic nation, whose proximity to Russia and unusually open public records system make it particularly vulnerable to Moscow’s hybrid war tactics.
For many internet users, the time-saving option of clicking “Accept cookies” while visiting some of Sweden’s most popular websites seemed mostly harmless. Even the companies hosting the websites thought so – to them, the ad-tech groups paying for the data-collecting cookies appeared to be legitimate.
But in at least one case, it was all a front.
In an investigation conducted by Swedish newspaper Dagens Nyheter (DN), potentially sensitive user information was shown to be collected – via a digital front in Luxembourg – and then funneled to a Moscow-based company partly financed by Russian oligarch Roman Abramovich.
Abramovich is the former owner of Chelsea FC and a close ally of Russian President Vladimir Putin. When Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, he was among the first oligarchs to be added to international sanctions lists, forcing him to sell the football club – the proceeds from which are still frozen in a British bank account.
Hundreds of websites
In its investigation, DN was able to trace traffic going from 425 Swedish websites directly to an Abramovich-linked company called Between Digital. Many of the websites, such as online directories Eniro and Hitta.se as well as several digital media platforms, are among Sweden’s most popular, and are used by people every day. Hitta.se, for example, says it registers some 400 million visits a year.
Carl Heath, a senior scientist at Sweden’s state-owned research institute RISE, told the newspaper that since Between Digital has its central server in Moscow, everything it gathers can be readily accessed by Russian authorities like the FSB domestic security and intelligence agency.
“Who looks up whom, from where and when is precisely the kind of data that could be of interest to a foreign power,” Heath explained, noting that the data obtained is much more detailed than simply IP addresses.
Home addresses, court records, dating habits
Some of the websites that Between Digital has been keeping tabs on are platforms that have built their whole business models on Sweden’s unusually far-reaching freedom of information principle.
The principle stipulates that all of Sweden’s official records, save those that have been specifically classified, are available to the public. In practice, this means that anyone can anonymously look up anything from a person’s home address and salary to their date of birth or any court ruling in which they were involved.
And a lot of it is now available online.
Ratsit.se, an online search engine and one of the websites targeted by Between Digital, provides much of this type of data, going as far as to list whether someone is married or what kind of car they own.
Jonas Lejon, a cybersecurity expert and founder of the IT security company Triop, said that the combination of the ability to track online behaviour as well as to extract so much personal information from public records is extremely dangerous.
“You can piece together the puzzle about people. You can profile them to the extent that you know exactly who they are,” he said.
“Ultimately, it could be used to pressure people through blackmail and other threats.”
Familjeliv.se, Sweden’s largest online community and parenting portal, has also been subject to Between Digital’s data collection. In just the past 30 days, the website registered nearly 2 million sessions – and considering that the country's population is under 11 million, that traffic is massive.
Many of the users turning to Familjeliv.se do use aliases to protect their identities, since the topics discussed can be sensitive and range from relationships to issues in the workplace.
‘We didn’t know’
So-called persistent cookies, or cookies designed to remain for longer than a specific online session, can trace a person’s internet activity for weeks or even months unless a user clears their browser cache (a folder that remembers websites the person has visited). The DN investigation did not reveal what type of cookies Between Digital is thought to be using, however.
Mikko Hypponen, recognised as one of Finland’s most prominent cybersecurity experts, said this type of data is a goldmine for intelligence agencies – which can now also use AI to help them extract useful information.
“Data is key to everything today. The more you have, the better, and it’s especially valuable for intelligence agencies and espionage purposes,” he said.
Even when cookies might not be able to determine exactly what a person is doing on a website, the visit in itself can be revealing.
“Let’s say you keep visiting a dating site late in the night, every night, or you go to the website of a psychotherapy centre once a week, or you visit the website for a dependency group like Alcoholics Anonymous. We may have no idea exactly what you did on the site, but we can guess,” Hypponen said.
User data has been misused before. As recently as October, Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli tech-ad firm had used advertising technology to install spyware on some of the media group’s devices. And in 2023, the Washington Post revealed that a conservative Catholic group in the United States spent millions of dollars to track the online behaviour of priests they suspected were gay.
Following DN’s investigation into Between Digital, many of the concerned websites have cut ties with the company and launched internal investigations.
“We didn’t know until you contacted us,” Gustav Kinde, the head of Ratsit, told the newspaper, echoing the reactions of many other company executives.

Usman Khawaja and David Warner were taken off television commentary duties on Saturday until the “Sandpap
items.text:
Usman Khawaja and David Warner taken off air over Australia’s Sandpapergate
Ex-Australia cricketers Khawaja and Warner taken off air having been most outspoken over 2018 scandal in South Africa.
Usman Khawaja and David Warner were taken off television commentary duties on Saturday until the “Sandpapergate” storm passes, with both set to miss Australia’s entire Twenty20 series against England.
The retired pair have been the centre of attention since Khawaja claimed in his autobiography more than two weeks ago that the whole team knew about the plot to alter the ball in a Test against South Africa in Cape Town in 2018.
Only then-captain Steve Smith, his deputy Warner and Cameron Bancroft – who used the sandpaper – were found to be responsible by a Cricket Australia probe.
The move by Fox Sports, for whom they both work, came after Cricket Australia threw its “unanimous support” behind embattled Test captain Pat Cummins.
Cummins denied he knew what was going on and has been under huge pressure since Khawaja’s claims, which were first backed by Warner and then Bancroft.
“In light of recent events, both Usman and Davey will be rested from our broadcasts over the next few weeks,” Fox Sports Managing Director Steve Crawley told Australian media.
“While we always support all members of our commentary team and welcome a diversity of views which is a feature of our summer of cricket, we also understand the pressure they are under to respond to each and every new comment.
“We think it is increasingly difficult to focus on the game while the situation continues to unfold and think it is unfair on both commentators to put them in that position.
“We will continue to monitor the situation,” Crawley said.
It was unclear when they would return, but Australia play four Tests against New Zealand in December-January after the five-game T20 series that got under way in Melbourne on Saturday.
Fast bowler Josh Hazlewood is the latest player from the 2018 side to deny any knowledge of the use of sandpaper and added on Saturday that he would have considered his future had Cummins been removed as captain.

COP31: UN Climate summit runs into overtime as deal remains elusive
Published November 20, 2026last updated November 21, 2026
What you need to know
- Diplomats and delegates from nearly 200 countries are meeting in Antalya, Turkey
- A new draft deal omits any mention of how to phase out fossil fuels, in what campaigners call a step 'backwards' and a 'glaring regression'
- Like in previous years, the climate summit has been extended until a consensus is reached
These are the major developments from the closing phase of the UN's COP31 Climate Summit in Antalya, Turkey, on Friday, November 20 and Saturday, November 21:
Peru blames 'geopolitical divisions' for lack of COP31 progress
The head of Peru's delegation at COP31, Andres Martin Garrido Sanchez, warned that the UN climate summit was unlikely to end with a concrete deal on climate financing or cutting fossil fuel use.
Garrido Sanchez lamented that the outcome "would be very limited."
He reiterated how "geopolitical divisions" were stopping any final deal from mentioning reducing reliance on oil, gas and coal.
The Peruvian delegate singled out major oil producers, such as Gulf Arab states and Russia, as showing significant opposition.
He noted that while Latin American neighbor Panama had also signaled objection to including the term fossil fuels in the final text, Peru was "not so radical" and is keen to attract investment to "ensure our energy security" through renewables.
China throws weight behind '35-by-35' pledge
China has backed a plan proposed by COP host Turkey to raise global electricity demand to 35% by 2035 — up from the current 20%.
In a joint statement with Australia, which is leading negotiations between almost 200 nations at the COP31 summit in Turkey, Beijing said it welcomes "growing international ambition and cooperation ... to increase electricity's share of global final energy consumption to 35 per cent by 2035 on a voluntary basis."
The statement goes on to highlight the benefits the transition can bring for the economy, jobs, energy security, public health and households.
The two partners also "acknowledge the importance of inclusive climate action that ensures no one is left behind," the text continued.
Dozens of countries, including EU states, Japan, South Korea and Canada, have so far signaled support for the voluntary goal, which aims to boost clean energy use.
Yet, environmental groups have warned that the draft text doesn't stipulate the use of solar, wind and other renewable energy sources, which could allow power plants using natural gas and coal to be included.
COP31: What to expect today
Good morning, and welcome back to DW's coverage of the UN's COP31 climate summit in Turkey.
Negotiators from nearly 200 countries worked through the night to finalize a deal, after a draft text dropped all mention of fossil fuels — the leading cause of climate change.
COP31, being held in the Mediterranean city of Antalya, was due to wrap up on Friday, but has run over time amid deep divisions over fossil fuels.
Hopes are fading that negotiators will finalize concrete plans to drastically slash the use of oil, gas and coal and a deeper commitment to renewable energy.
Stay tuned as we bring you the latest from the closing stages of UN climate summit.
COP31 talks go on — we're taking a break
The UN climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, has gone into overtime, with countries still divided over key issues, including fossil fuels and climate financing.
The talks were scheduled to end on Friday evening, but negotiators have yet to reach an agreement. Germany and several other countries are pushing for a clear commitment to phase out fossil fuels, while poorer nations are demanding more concrete financial support to cope with climate change.
Negotiations are expected to continue into the weekend. We are pausing our live coverage for now and will bring you further updates as talks progress.
WATCH — Turkey's beaches are becoming too hot for sea turtles
While Turkey hosts COP31 in Antalya, a growing climate threat is unfolding on its Mediterranean beaches. Rising sand temperatures are causing most newly hatched sea turtles to be born female, raising concerns about the long-term survival of local populations.
Conservationists warn that climate change, combined with pollution, coastal development and fishing-related injuries, is putting increasing pressure on the species.
DW correspondent Julia Hahn follows the people working to protect Turkey's iconic loggerhead turtles and shows how the climate crisis is already affecting wildlife far beyond the COP31 conference halls.
WATCH — COP climate summit under scrutiny over fossil fuel influence
The UN climate summit in Antalya is drawing criticism from activists and campaigners who question whether global climate talks can deliver meaningful change while fossil fuel interests remain influential. Turkey and Australia, both under scrutiny for their energy policies, are leading this year's conference.
Activists, including Greta Thunberg, argue COP summits have become increasingly ineffective, while others defend them as a vital space to pressure governments. Climate policy experts say the talks have helped reduce projected warming, but stress that real progress depends on action taken by countries between summits, not just agreements reached at them.
WATCH — Maldives environment minister: 'We are not going to live in the dark'
For the Maldives, climate change is already affecting everyday life. Heavy rainfall has forced people from their homes, warmer oceans are damaging coral reefs, and changes in fish stocks are putting pressure on the country's fishing industry. Rising sea levels pose another threat to the low-lying island nation. Meanwhile, global greenhouse gas emissions continue to rise, despite more than three decades of international climate negotiations.

In a statement shared through his official office, Kenyatta conveyed his sympathies to the South African government and people
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 21 — Former President Uhuru Kenyatta has sent a condolence message to South Africa following the death of former Deputy President Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka.
In a statement shared through his official office, Kenyatta conveyed his sympathies to the South African government and people, as well as the family of the late former Deputy President.
Kenyatta remembered Mlambo-Ngcuka as a distinguished leader whose service to South Africa and contribution to advancing gender equality and women’s empowerment had left an enduring legacy.
The former Head of State also prayed for strength, comfort and courage for her family and the people of South Africa as they come to terms with the loss.
Mlambo-Ngcuka’s death was announced by the South African Presidency on Friday, November 20, with Acting President Paul Mashatile conveying condolences to her family on behalf of the government and the people of the country.
She served as South Africa’s Deputy President from 2005 to 2008, becoming the first woman to hold the position.
She later served as United Nations Under-Secretary-General and Executive Director of UN Women between 2013 and 2021, where she championed gender equality and the empowerment of women and girls.
Her death has drawn tributes from across Africa and the international community, with leaders and organisations recognising her contribution to public service, women’s rights and social justice.

The President said parents should no longer be expected to pay teachers, arguin
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 21 – President William Ruto has announced plans to absorb teachers employed by school Boards of Management (BOMs) into the Government payroll, in a move aimed at easing the financial burden on parents.
The President said parents should no longer be expected to pay teachers, arguing that the responsibility of employing and remunerating educators rests with the Government.
“I want all teachers employed by Boards of Management placed on Government payroll. Parents should not continue paying for teachers because that is the responsibility of the Government,” he said.
Ruto spoke at Kipsigon in Mount Elgon Constituency, Bungoma County, on the third day of his development tour of the Western region.
He said the directive forms part of his administration’s affirmative action measures aimed at promoting equity and ensuring learners across the country have equal access to quality education, regardless of their backgrounds.
The Head of State noted that the Government had employed 100,000 teachers over the past four years and would recruit an additional 20,000 next month.
He also highlighted investments in education infrastructure, saying the Government had constructed 23,000 classrooms countrywide to ease congestion and improve the learning environment.
On land ownership, the President reaffirmed his commitment to resolving longstanding disputes in Mount Elgon, where residents have faced challenges securing legal ownership of land.
During the visit, he issued 1,845 title deeds to beneficiaries of the Chepyuk Settlement Scheme Phase III, with a further 2,000 title deeds for Phase II in the pipeline.
“We will make sure that no Kenyan continues living like a squatter in their own country,” he said.
Ruto challenged leaders overseeing settlement schemes to resolve internal disputes and facilitate the issuance of ownership documents to deserving beneficiaries.
The President also cautioned young people against being exploited by politicians to engage in criminal activities or advance political interests.
“Don’t agree to be misused by politicians to commit crimes or engage in blogging for them,” he said.
He instead urged the youth to take advantage of Government empowerment programmes to develop their skills and access economic opportunities.
On the forthcoming General Election, Ruto accused opposition leaders of attempting to undermine the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) through what he termed unnecessary demands.
He argued that the demands reflected a lack of confidence in their electoral prospects, insisting that the electoral agency and other institutions were staffed by competent Kenyans who should be allowed to discharge their mandates.
“If you want to work in the IEBC, apply. If you wanted to be procurement officers, you should have applied so that you know where ballot papers will be procured from. Those institutions are run by competent Kenyans and we must respect them,” he said.
National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang’ula expressed confidence that Ruto would secure overwhelming support from Bungoma and the wider Western Kenya region in the next General Election.
Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi also voiced confidence in the President’s re-election prospects, declaring: “We want the two terms without a petition.”
Mudavadi credited Ruto with initiating what he described as an infrastructure revolution in the country.
Bungoma Governor Kenneth Lusaka commended the President for what he termed the equitable distribution of development projects across the country, saying the approach would strengthen his political support ahead of the elections.
Later, in Sirisia Constituency, Ruto launched the construction of a modern market and addressed residents in Sirisia town.

items.text:
Demolition notices for buildings in Hebron provoke fear among Palestinians
Palestinians fear forced displacement as Israeli authorities target legally licensed homes in a Palestinian-administered area of the occupied West Bank.
Hebron, Occupied West Bank – Amjad al-Qawasmi stood gazing at the eight-storey residential building he constructed 13 years ago in the heart of Hebron. He struggled to understand how it could be reduced to rubble in a matter of moments.
The building in the southern West Bank is one of two upon which the Israeli army posted demolition notices last Sunday morning, even though both are in Area A, which, under the Oslo Accords, is under full Palestinian control.
The buildings are in the Dairat al-Seer area, in the northwest of Hebron. One contains 25 residential apartments, the other has 40, alongside an adjacent home. The Israeli army has set a one-week deadline for filing objections to the demolition orders.
The Israeli authorities justified the decisions by citing the buildings’ proximity to “Settler Road 35”, despite the structures possessing all the necessary permits from the Palestinian Authority and the Hebron Municipality.
Hebron is divided into a larger area under Palestinian administrative control and a smaller area – housing Israeli settlers – in the centre of the city.
Pervasive fear
The affected families are living in a state of anxiety, fearing that the demolition orders will be carried out. Meanwhile, the property owners have filed formal objections in an attempt to halt the demolitions.
Al-Qawasmi told Al Jazeera that his building was constructed in 2013 at a cost exceeding 18 million shekels ($5.6m). He, along with his father and brother, had prepared the apartments for occupancy from the ground up, installing all necessary utilities after obtaining the required permits from the Ministry of Local Government.
He explained that he, his brothers, and their families live on the lower floors of the building.
Most of the other apartments were sold to families who have yet to complete their payments; a situation exacerbated by the difficult economic conditions they are facing, such as salary cuts and the ban on most Palestinian workers entering Israel for employment, which has been in effect since the October 7, 2023 attack on Israel and the start of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza.
“Like all the residents of the building, we fear the execution of the demolition order. Although we have hired a lawyer to try to freeze the decision, this is an occupation, anything is possible,” said al-Qawasmi.
The families living in the two buildings have begun packing their essential belongings and clothing into cardboard boxes in anticipation of a potential forced eviction to carry out the demolition. However, they remain uncertain about the fate of their furniture and other possessions, should they not be granted the time to clear out their apartments.
A devastating loss
Samer Abu Hadid purchased a plot of land in the area five years ago and built a villa for his eight-member family. The 1,165 square metre property cost an estimated $3m.
Last Sunday morning, he was shocked when Israeli soldiers stormed the villa and served him a demolition notice, granting him a one-week window to file an objection. The order stated that it was a military decision based on “security grounds”.
“I told the officer that the villa is legally licensed and there are no grounds for its demolition. He simply replied, ‘Look at the document carefully, the reasons are security-related ‘ and added that I have one week to file an objection. But what can I possibly do in one week against an already-issued demolition order?” he asked Al Jazeera.
Abu Hadid reached out to local authorities to follow up on the matter, yet he remains deeply concerned that the demolition order might actually be carried out.
“We literally cannot sleep any more; we think about this constantly. We don’t know whether we should move out our furniture and empty the villa, or stay put. Nothing is clear, and we are at a loss as to what to do,” he said.
Blow to the investment sector
According to a report by the UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (covering the period from November 2024 to October 2025), Israel targeted 97 Palestinian structures in Area A either through actual demolition or the issuance of demolition orders. This is in addition to 46 structures in Area B, 1,390 in Area C and 240 in occupied East Jerusalem.
The Palestinian Commission Against the Wall and Settlements has documented the issuance of 9,518 demolition or ‘stop-construction’ notices between 2015 and the end of September 2026.
They include 344 notices issued during the first nine months of this year. Hebron governorate tops the list with 2,697 notices issued in the city.
Hebron Municipal Council member Muammar al-Oweiwi told Al Jazeera that the recent demolition notices set a precedent in Hebron by targeting Area A, which should be under the full civil and security control of the Palestinian National Authority. Demolition and stop-construction orders were also issued for a family guesthouse and another building in the Farsh al-Hawa area in Area C.
Al-Oweiwi said that the Hebron Municipality is addressing the matter, in coordination with the property owners’ lawyers, by submitting documentation, including building permits, and pursuing the necessary legal procedures.
He added that the case is now before the Israeli courts; the lawyers requested an immediate stay or freeze on the demolition orders, but Israel has yet to respond.
“The municipality is not merely seeking to freeze the decision, but to have it overturned entirely and to secure official documentation confirming that the demolition of these buildings is unlawful,” he stated.

items.text:
Anthropic researcher uses AI to solve math's greatest riddle
November 21, 2026
A mathematician working for AI giant Anthropic says he used the company's Claude AI tool to solve one of mathematics most famous problems.
The Riemann hypothesis dates back to 1859 and centers on the distribution of prime numbers underpinning a much wider scope of mathematical work.
Levent Alpoge, a member of Anthropic's technical staff, made the announcement on his website. "I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis," Levent Alpoge wrote in a note released Friday.
The proof still has to be verified and confirmed by other mathematicians. If it withstands independent examination, it would be a major milestone both in mathematics and the growing role of artificial intelligence (AI) in scientific research.
The Riemann hypothesis is the latest and most important in a string of famous mathematical problems that were tackled with the help of AI.
What did Alpoge say about the breakthrough?
Alpoge said that the collaboration with AI had generated more than 250,000 pages of mathematical material, adding that he had not yet mastered all the mathematics involved.
"Claude and I have had a great time together with such breadth in recent months, but this time Claude far outpaced me near the finish line," he wrote. "No, Claude flew, and danced, and sparkled near that finish line."
The Riemann Hypothesis is one of seven major mathematical problems, the so-called Millennium Prize Problems, selected by the Clay Mathematics Institute, which offers $1 million for a solution to each of those.
"This is an announcement of historic significance," Martin Bridson, president of the institute, said in a statement quoted by news agency AP.
He added it "holds the promise of a dramatic transformation in the perception of what is possible in the struggle to extend the human understanding of mathematics."
"But the journey from today’s announcement to a place of real understanding will be long and difficult."
What is the Riemann hypothesis?
Formulated by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann in the 19th century, the hypothesis is about the distribution of prime numbers, which are numbers that can only be divided by themselves and the number 1.
The hypothesis describes a fundamental pattern of how these numbers are distributed as they become ever larger. Confirming that hypothesis is thought to have crucial implications for a wide range of further mathematical research.
The potential breakthrough by Alpoge and Claude AI comes amid a growing number of examples where artificial intelligence systems are making significant contributions to advanced mathematical research.
In September, rival AI company OpenAI said its technology had helped solve a problem involving the Navier-Stokes equations.
The equations, which describe the movement of fluids such as water and air, are another of the seven Millennium Prize Problems, but the claim that they've been solved also still needs independent verification.

James Harden scored a season-high 51 points – moving into third place in NBA history with his 26th career 50-point
items.text:
Cavaliers’ Harden passes Bryant, closes on Jordan in NBA 50-point game list
James Harden climbs NBA career record list in leading Cleveland Cavaliers to 128-119 win over Indiana Pacers.
James Harden scored a season-high 51 points – moving into third place in NBA history with his 26th career 50-point game – while leading the Cleveland Cavaliers to a 128-119 win over the visiting Indiana Pacers.
Harden, 37, made 15 of 26 field-goal attempts, 7 of 11 3-point shots and all 14 of his free throws while breaking a tie with Kobe Bryant on the 50-point list. Wilt Chamberlain holds the NBA record with 118 50-point games, and Michael Jordan is second with 31.
Donovan Mitchell added 20 points for Cleveland on a night when all NBA games were part of the NBA Cup’s group stage. The Cavaliers earned their third win in the past four games overall.
Pascal Siakam and Ivica Zubac each scored 21 for Indiana, which took its third consecutive loss.
Atlanta Hawks 111, Charlotte Hornets 97
Jalen Johnson compiled 26 points, six rebounds and six assists to help Atlanta post a victory over visiting Charlotte.
Aaron Wiggins scored 19 points, and Nickeil Alexander-Walker added 17 for the Hawks, who won their third straight game and their seventh in nine tries. Atlanta trailed by 14 points in the first half.
Moussa Diabate produced 21 points and 15 rebounds while Brandon Miller scored 19 points for the Hornets, who lost their fourth straight game.
Orlando Magic 113, Brooklyn Nets 111
Franz Wagner capped a stellar 35-point performance with a tiebreaking stepback jumper over two defenders with 2.8 seconds left as Orlando outlasted Brooklyn in New York.
Wagner made 13 of 25 shots as the Magic beat the Nets for the 10th straight time. Orlando’s Desmond Bane hit seven 3-pointers for his 21 points.
Julius Randle collected 27 points, nine rebounds and six assists for the Nets, but he missed a last-second 3-point attempt. Day’Ron Sharpe contributed 17 points and 11 boards as Brooklyn took its fourth loss in a row.
Toronto Raptors 105, Detroit Pistons 102
Scottie Barnes had 29 points, including a go-ahead basket in the final minute, and visiting Toronto snapped a six-game losing streak by edging Detroit.
Raptors rookie Allen Graves, making his first start, supplied career highs of 20 points and 10 rebounds while Immanuel Quickley notched 18 points and 10 assists.
Cade Cunningham totalled 23 points and nine assists as the Pistons took just their second loss in six games. Kevin Huerter added 20 points.
Oklahoma City Thunder 126, New Orleans Pelicans 120
Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored 40 points to lead Oklahoma City past visiting New Orleans, just the Thunder’s second win in the past six games.
Rookie Aday Mara had career highs of 22 points and 16 rebounds for Oklahoma City. The Thunder shot 53.3% from the field, their second-best effort of the season.
Zion Williamson and Jeremiah Fears each scored 22 points for the Pelicans, who took their eighth loss in nine games.
Denver Nuggets 133, Houston Rockets 124
Nikola Jokic had 24 of his 26 points after halftime and added 11 assists as host Denver overcame a triple-double by Alperen Sengun to beat Houston.
Christian Braun and Cameron Johnson scored 19 points each for the Nuggets, who won their second straight contest. The game featured 32 lead changes, the most in the NBA this season.
Sengun finished with 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists for the Rockets, who had won five of their previous six games. Fred VanVleet put up 25 points.
Los Angeles Lakers 106, Sacramento Kings 104
Luka Doncic scored 25 points and dished out eight assists as Los Angeles rallied past visiting Sacramento, avoiding what would have been the Lakers’ first set of consecutive losses this season.
Walker Kessler added 15 points as the Lakers came out on top after their nine-game winning streak ended Wednesday in a loss to the Utah Jazz.
De’Andre Hunter scored 30 points, and Domantas Sabonis added 19 points and 16 rebounds as the Kings dropped their eighth straight game. Sacramento led by as many as 11 points in the third quarter.
Washington Wizards 98, Chicago Bulls 94
Anthony Davis finished with game highs of 36 points and 11 rebounds as Washington rallied from a 15-point deficit to down host Chicago.
Davis also made a key play on defence when he disrupted Norman Powell’s potential game-tying layup attempt with six seconds remaining to force a miss. Wizards rookie AJ Dybantsa posted 20 points, 10 rebounds and six assists.
Powell led the Bulls with 16 points but shot just 7 of 18. Buddy Hield contributed 15 points off the bench.
Phoenix Suns 111, Utah Jazz 101
Devin Booker scored 23 points, Dillon Brooks and Miles Bridges added 18 apiece, and Phoenix ran its winning streak to three with a victory over Utah in Salt Lake City.
Collin Gillespie added 16 points and three 3-pointers off the bench, and Jalen Green scored 14 for the Suns, who have won five of seven. At 8-7, Phoenix is over .500 for the first time this season.
Rookie Darryn Peterson had 20 points and set his season highs in rebounds (10) and assists (eight) while recording his first career double-double. Jaxson Hayes added 18 points and a season-best 14 boards for the Jazz, who had won their previous two after a 1-13 start.
