items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 21 – Embakasi East MP Babu Owino has claimed he contributed 99.9 per cent to Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna’s political growth, insisting their relationship remains intact despite disagreements over the leadership of the Linda Mwananchi political outfit.
Babu described Sifuna as his brother and maintained that he still wants to see him rise to the country’s top political office, dismissing suggestions that their individual ambitions have put them on a collision course.
Speaking during an interview, the legislator said he had played a central role in Sifuna’s political journey and had no intention of standing in the way of his ambitions.
“Edwin Sifuna is my brother. I have contributed 99.9 per cent in his growth, and I still want him to grow,” Babu said.
He said the two leaders had different political ambitions that could be accommodated within the same movement, with Sifuna pursuing the presidency and himself seeking the Nairobi governorship in the 2027 General Election.
“Within Linda Mwananchi movement, he’s our presidential candidate. Babu is the next governor of Nairobi. There’s no problem if we both grow,” he added.
His remarks come amid a disagreement over the political party structure and leadership arrangement within Linda Mwananchi, with the two leaders giving different accounts of the understanding reached during the formation of the outfit.
Speaking on Citizen TV Radio, Sifuna explained that the original arrangement involved leaders bringing their individual political parties together under one political vehicle, initially known as The Equitable Party (TEP).
The senator said five leaders had presented their respective parties for consideration before a committee was established to assess their suitability and organisational structures.
He maintained that the group eventually settled on TEP and that he was subsequently entrusted with the position of party leader as well as the presidential ticket.
Sifuna questioned the objections to his position as party leader, arguing that it was inconsistent for colleagues to trust him with the presidential candidature but not with the leadership of the party.
“Niambie chama kimoja ambacho mgombea wa Rais sio kinara wa chama. Unaniamini kuwa Rais wa nchi lakini sio Party Leader wa chama?” he posed.
The senator also defended himself against accusations of going against the original agreement, challenging those questioning the arrangement to explain where he had betrayed the group’s understanding.
He further said some members later preferred to retain their individual political parties rather than consolidate under a single outfit.
Babu, however, insists that having a separate political vehicle does not amount to abandoning Linda Mwananchi, describing the Mwananchi Party as part of the wider movement.
“Mwananchi Party is part of Linda Mwananchi movement. It’s been built through sweat, tears and blood of Kenyans,” he said.
The MP described himself as a key stakeholder in the movement, arguing that different political vehicles could help accommodate supporters who identify with different leaders.
He said some Kenyans support Sifuna, others are aligned with him, while another section backs both politicians, making it necessary to have structures that accommodate the different political interests.
“There are people who like Sifuna and don’t like Babu and vice versa. Some like both of us. People who don’t like him, won’t they go to him through Babu Owino? And they need a vehicle,” he said.
Babu maintained that the question of party ownership and leadership should be addressed through negotiations, insisting that the emerging differences should not be interpreted as a breakdown of his political relationship with Sifuna.
The two leaders are among politicians associated with Linda Mwananchi who are seeking to consolidate their political positions ahead of the 2027 General Election.

items.title: Kindiki Warns Politicians Against Divisive Rhetoric Ahead of 2027 General Election
items.summary:
NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 21 – Deputy President Kithure Kindiki has urged politicians to avoid divisive rhetoric and incitement to violence ahead of the 2027 General Election, warning that ethnic mobilisation could undermine national unity and trigger conflict.
Kindiki cautioned against political leaders w
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 21 – Deputy President Kithure Kindiki has urged politicians to avoid divisive rhetoric and incitement to violence ahead of the 2027 General Election, warning that ethnic mobilisation could undermine national unity and trigger conflict.
Kindiki cautioned against political leaders who exploit ethnic differences and promote negative narratives for political gain, saying such actions threatened the stability of a country with more than 55 million people.
Speaking in the Kiratina area of Nakuru Town East during a development tour, the Deputy President urged Kenyans not to allow a small number of politicians seeking elective positions to plunge the country into chaos.
“These politicians are vying for not more than 2,000 elective seats and we cannot allow them to cause conflicts for all the 55 million of us,” he said.
Accompanied by Nakuru Governor Susan Kihika, Nakuru Town East MP David Gikaria and Nakuru Woman Representative Lisa Chelule, Kindiki said political competition should not translate into enmity, adding that the best candidates should win through a democratic process.
He challenged politicians to focus on selling their policies, development plans and track records instead of exploiting ethnic, religious and political differences.
“Political competition should be anchored on ideas and constructive debate. The electioneering period will be short-lived and the country is bigger than any one person or political party,” he said.
Kindiki also called on politicians to tone down their internal and external party disagreements, insisting that Kenya must remain peaceful and safe for all citizens.
Addressing competition among aspirants within the ruling United Democratic Alliance (UDA), he urged them to conduct their campaigns peacefully and avoid using supporters to settle political scores.
“We have very many aspirants within the United Democratic Alliance (UDA), keep the competition civil, do not trade insults and use the people in your fights. The best candidate will take the ticket and the party will find a way of including the rest,” he said.
He added that UDA was engaging stakeholders to consolidate support ahead of the 2027 General Election, saying the party intended to campaign on the strength of its ideology.
On development, Kindiki said the government had invested close to Sh100 billion in Nakuru County through infrastructure projects targeting roads, affordable housing, student hostels and modern markets.
He said the government was constructing 830 kilometres of tarmac roads in the county at a cost of more than Sh38 billion.
An additional Sh47 billion, he said, had been set aside for affordable housing, student hostels and modern markets.
Kindiki also announced that a major section of the Lironi-Mau Summit dual carriageway, stretching from Limuru through Kimende to Naivasha, was expected to be completed within the next two months.
“A large section of the Lironi-Mau Summit dual carriageway running from Limuru, through Kimende all the way to Naivasha will be complete in the next two months,” he said.
He observed that the projects would transform the county’s economy and improve Nakuru City’s overall outlook.

items.text:
'Killer robots' talks at UN end with no legally binding ban
November 21, 2026
United Nations talks on regulating lethal autonomous weapons systems ended on Saturday without an agreement on a legally binding ban.
The negotiations did, however, yield an agreement for further discussions to develop new rules by 2028.
Delegates from 128 states that are parties to the UN Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons (CCW) had been meeting in Geneva since Monday amid rising concerns over the use of the so-called killer robots in global conflicts.
The conference ended early on Saturday in what campaigners deemed a "weakened" outcome, following several hours of overnight parleying.
What happened at the CCW conference?
Nearly 100 nations had called for negotiations on a legally binding agreement on the systems capable of killing without a human making the final decision to fire.
UN Secretary-General António Guterres, Pope Leo XIV and the Red Cross had also supported a ban on killer robots.
However, countries that have the technology, including arms-producing giants like the US, Russia and Israel, were among those opposing the mandate.
Ultimately, the 128 countries "agreed to launch the elaboration of an international instrument on lethal autonomous weapons systems, which should be conducted over the next two years", the conference's Swiss chair, Julien Thoni, told the media on Saturday.
Groups decry a softened mandate on 'killer robots'
But while Thoni hailed a multilateral diplomacy delivering "concrete results" even in "today's deeply divided world," rights groups expressed disappointment at the minimal agreement.
"States adopted a watered-down mandate that fails to chart a clear path towards a legally binding instrument," news agency AFP quoted Stop Killer Robots, a global coalition of over 300 organizations, as saying.
"Over 95 states expressed their support for a treaty. In the final hours, a small number of states weakened the mandate introducing uncertainty about the legal status of the final document," it added.
The group had earlier said that autonomous weapons systems were already reaching the battlefield and such systems had been tested or deployed, including in the Ukraine war.

items.summary:
NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 21 – Public Health Principal Secretary Mary Muthoni has urged parents to closely monitor their children during the school holidays, warning against drug and substance abuse and other risky behaviours among young people.
Muthoni also called for strict adherence to hygiene standards
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 21 – Public Health Principal Secretary Mary Muthoni has urged parents to closely monitor their children during the school holidays, warning against drug and substance abuse and other risky behaviours among young people.
Muthoni also called for strict adherence to hygiene standards and established medical procedures during circumcision ceremonies, cautioning those involved against negligence that could endanger the lives of boys undergoing the rite of passage.
She emphasised that proper hygiene and compliance with medical guidelines were critical in safeguarding the health and safety of initiates.
The PS further urged parents to remain actively involved in their children’s lives during the holiday period by monitoring their whereabouts, social circles and activities.
She warned that school holidays expose young people to various risks, including drug and substance abuse, and called on families to protect children from negative influences.
Muthoni particularly cautioned candidates who had completed their Kenya Certificate of Secondary Education (KCSE) examinations against engaging in drugs and other harmful behaviours as they transition into adulthood.
She noted that although completing secondary education gives young people greater freedom, it also comes with increased responsibility.
The PS also urged Kenyans to prioritise safety during the festive season, highlighting the importance of food safety, responsible consumption and the security of families and communities.
On development in Kirinyaga County, Muthoni highlighted ongoing and completed government projects, including affordable housing in Kianyaga and road construction across various sub-counties.
She cited the completed affordable housing project in Kianyaga and the Mwea-Gichugu Belt Road as examples of development initiatives being implemented under President William Ruto’s administration.
The PS also highlighted youth empowerment and small business support programmes, saying young people from every ward had benefited from grants under the National Youth Opportunities Towards Advancement (NYOTA) programme.
She said 70 youths from each ward had received Sh50,000 grants to establish businesses, emphasising that the funds were grants and not loans.
According to Muthoni, beneficiaries were also being equipped with information and skills to access government procurement opportunities and expand their enterprises.
She encouraged women, young people and persons living with disabilities to familiarise themselves with government procurement procedures to benefit from the 30 per cent allocation reserved for these groups.

items.title: French police officers guilty of Michel Zecler assault: What happens now?
items.summary:

items.text:
French police officers guilty of Michel Zecler assault: What happens now?
Officers dealt more than 30 blows to the Black music producer in what the court ruled was a racially motivated crime.
A French court has found three French police officers guilty of intentional, racist violence during the 2020 assault of Michel Zecler, a Black music producer, and sentenced them to prison.
The landmark ruling has once again shone a spotlight on the issue of police brutality in France, which activists say is rarely prosecuted despite being systemic and often racially motivated.
Here’s what happened in the case and what it means now:
What was the verdict?
The Paris criminal court convicted three police officers of assaulting Zecler in Paris in 2020, ruling that the attack was racially motivated. The court also found the defendants guilty of falsifying a police report about the incident.
The officers – 29-year-old Aurelien Lapersonne, 50-year-old Philippe Tondeux and 37-year-old Pierre Plantier – were each sentenced to five years in prison, part of which was suspended.
All three have been barred from serving in the police force again.
Who is Michel Zecler?
Zecler is a 47-year-old French music producer who co-founded the independent rap label Black Gold Corp. Zecler has worked in the French hip-hop industry for years, including helping to put together the prominent 2016 rap tour called L’Age d’Or du Rap Francais.
Music journalist Olivier Cachin described Zecler as easy-going and humble. “He just works, staying very much in the background,” Cachin told French newspaper Sud Ouest. “He’s not a ‘look-at-me’ type… He’s just a big teddy bear.”
Why was Zecler beaten by the French police?
Officers stopped Zecler outside his Paris music studio on November 21, 2020, accusing him of failing to put on a compulsory face mask, as required by France’s COVID-19 restrictions at the time.
The officers then pushed Zecler back into the building and assaulted him – an incident captured by his security cameras.
Over five minutes or so, the officers punched, kicked and used batons to deliver some 30 blows to Zecler, severely injuring him. He suffered head trauma and a complete rupture of his biceps tendon.
Zecler said the officers repeatedly used a racist slur during the beating, and that the assault had left him “completely devastated”.
What happened during the trial?
Officers Lapersonne, Paltier and Tondeux were found guilty of aggravated group assault that was racially motivated.
They were also convicted of falsifying an official police report in which they accused Zecler of being violent towards them – claims unsupported by the security footage.
The presiding judge said the officers had been dishonest in their report “to shield (themselves) from disciplinary and legal consequences, with no regard for the criminal consequences faced by Michel Zecler”.
Officer Lapersonne, who submitted the report, initially claimed that Zecler had attacked the officers and “struck out with his arms and legs”. When the presiding judge asked if he had “made that up”, Lapersonne responded during the trial, “Absolutely.” Lapersonne’s initial police report also failed to mention that the officers landed blows on Zecler.
“I deliberately omitted them. I think out of fear. It was stupid of me,” Lapersonne told the court.
All three of the convicted officers admitted to having used excessive force and apologised to Zecler, though they denied the charges of racism.
Tondeux, the oldest of the officers, said he regretted “the image I have given of the police”.
The judges said Zecler’s testimony, in which he claimed to have heard one of the officers use the racial slur “sale negre”, had been consistent from the beginning, while the officers’ falsified report damaged their credibility.
Speaking to the court, Zecler said he would likely not have been recognised as a victim if not for the security footage recording the incident.
How long have the French police officers been sentenced to prison?
All three were given five-year sentences, but with varying portions suspended.
Lapersonne, who was found to have first stopped Zecler and authored the falsified police report, had three years of his sentence suspended, while Tondeux had three and a half years suspended. Plantier had four years suspended and will serve the remaining year under electronic monitoring rather than in prison.
Zecler’s lawyer described the sentences as “falling short”, but said they set an important precedent.
“This precedent shows that even if a police officer lies, someone who comes forward to say the police did the worst to them can be believed,” said the lawyer.
What does the Michel Zecler case reveal about police brutality in France?
Zecler’s case is the latest to draw attention to the issue of police brutality in France, which is rarely prosecuted, as well as racial discrimination, following several high-profile cases in recent years.
In 2023, protests and riots broke out after Nahel Merzouk, a 17-year-old boy of North African descent, was shot and killed by a police officer during a traffic stop outside Paris. Police initially reported that an officer had shot at him because the teenager was driving his car at him, but this version of events was contradicted by a video circulating on social media. In March, a French appeals court ruled that the officer who shot Merzouk should stand trial.
In 2024, a judge handed suspended prison sentences to three officers who caused permanent rectal injuries to a Black man, Theo Luhaka, during a stop-and-search in 2017.
In 2016, Adama Traore, a 24-year-old man of Malian descent, died in custody after being restrained and apprehended by police following a dispute over an identity check. A case against three arresting police officers was dropped in 2023 and, in February this year, France’s top court, the Court of Cassation, ruled against reopening the investigation.

items.summary:
Harry Kane to miss ‘a few months’ after injury as Bayern Munich draw
Ballon d’Or winner tears a ligament in his left ankle during Bayern Munich’s 1-1 draw against Cologne.
England football captain Harry Kane will miss the “next few months” after tearing a ligament in his left ankle during Bayern Mun
items.text:
Harry Kane to miss ‘a few months’ after injury as Bayern Munich draw
Ballon d’Or winner tears a ligament in his left ankle during Bayern Munich’s 1-1 draw against Cologne.
England football captain Harry Kane will miss the “next few months” after tearing a ligament in his left ankle during Bayern Munich’s 1-1 draw against Cologne on Friday.
Kane was taken down in the area by Cologne defender Joel Schmied, who reached Michael Olise’s low cross first but knocked into the Ballon d’Or winner’s left leg in his follow-through at the back post.
Kane writhed in pain. Although he gingerly got back to his feet and initially continued playing, he soon hobbled off the field with two physiotherapists after treatment.
A club statement on X said: “Harry Kane suffered a tear of the syndesmosis ligament in his left ankle in Bayern Munich’s Bundesliga home match against Köln on Friday evening. This was confirmed by an examination by Bayern Munich’s medical department. The 33-year-old will therefore be out for the next few months.”
Kane is the undisputed star of Bayern. Since joining from Spurs in 2023, he has scored 156 goals in 161 competitive fixtures and won two Bundesliga titles and the German Cup.
He became the first Englishman to win the Ballon d’Or in 25 years last month and, two weeks ago, signed a new contract with Bayern that will keep him in Bavaria until June 2029.
The night was supposed to be a happy one for Bayern, who welcomed coach Vincent Kompany back to the dugout a month after he collapsed while watching the reserve squad train.
However, Kompany saw his team go behind after just 11 minutes when winger Mikey Moore, on loan from Tottenham, started and finished a counterattack.
Just nine minutes later, Kane limped off to be replaced by Tom Bischof, and the German midfielder made a quick impact. Before halftime, he found Nathaniel Brown, who fired a fierce shot into the bottom corner from the edge of the box.
Both sides had chances in a busy second half but it remained goalless and the point was enough for Bayern to edge a point ahead of Borussia Dortmund. Bayern remained the only unbeaten team in Europe’s top five leagues.
Cologne, for which Moore was named man of the match, climbed one place into 14th.

items.summary:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 21 — The Nairobi Hospital Chief Executive Officer Felix Osano has resigned, paving the way for the appointment of Magdalene Wambui Kamande as acting CEO amid prolonged boardroom wrangles and governance disputes at the institution.
Kamande, who previously served as the hospital’s
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 21 — The Nairobi Hospital Chief Executive Officer Felix Osano has resigned, paving the way for the appointment of Magdalene Wambui Kamande as acting CEO amid prolonged boardroom wrangles and governance disputes at the institution.
Kamande, who previously served as the hospital’s Director of ICT and Transformation Services, was appointed by the Board of Management during a meeting held on Friday, November 20.
In an internal memorandum addressed to staff and the Admitting Staff Association, Board Chairman Barcley Onyambu announced that Kamande’s appointment took effect immediately and would remain in force until further notice or as determined by the board.
“The Board of Management sitting today, 20th November, 2026, appointed Dr. Magdalene Wambui Kamande (Director ICT and Transformation Services) as the Acting Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of The Nairobi Hospital, with immediate effect,” the memo stated.
The board said Kamande would assume the responsibilities and functions of the chief executive in accordance with the hospital’s governance framework, established policies and procedures, and the authority delegated to the office.
Staff and members of the Admitting Staff Association were also urged to accord her the necessary support as she assumes leadership of the institution.
Her appointment comes against the backdrop of a prolonged leadership crisis at the hospital and its parent body, the Kenya Hospital Association (KHA), which owns and operates the facility.
The institution has been embroiled in competing claims over the legitimacy of its leadership, disputes surrounding board appointments and court battles that have attracted parliamentary and investigative attention.
In August, the association reconstituted its 11-member Board of Management following an annual general meeting held on August 25, with Onyambu retaining the chairmanship. Four new members were elected as part of the changes.
In October, the Consumer Federation of Kenya (COFEK) raised concerns over the registration of directors, compliance with court orders and the governance of the association.
COFEK Secretary-General Stephen Mutoro publicly highlighted the concerns, citing claims made by lawyers representing doctors involved in the dispute.
Osano was appointed acting chief executive in January 2025 following the exit of James Nyamongo, whose contract ended in December 2024.
Established in 1954, The Nairobi Hospital is a major tertiary referral facility offering specialist medical services. Its 2023 annual report indicated a capacity of more than 460 beds, six outpatient centres and a global medical evacuation centre.
Kamande now assumes executive leadership as the hospital navigates its latest management transition, with the board yet to indicate the duration of her acting appointment.

items.text:
Illicit alcohol kills 11, poisons 180 in northeast India’s Manipur state
Manipur’s chief minister orders a probe into the incident, saying those responsible will be arrested and punished.
At least 11 people have died after drinking what authorities suspect was spurious alcohol in northeast India’s Manipur state, prompting an investigation.
More than 180 people, who were believed to have consumed toxic liquor, had been admitted to hospitals in Manipur as of Friday.
According to local media, officials have advised locals who have drunk alcohol from Sugnu town in Manipur in the past week to seek medical evaluation. Meanwhile, the deputy police commissioner has advised people not to drink alcohol of unknown origin.
“Over 180 patients have been admitted in the two hospitals so far, while the death toll has reached 11 in the last 48 hours,” Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh said in a statement on Friday.
Illicit alcohol is a lucrative industry in India, attracting customers who are too poor to afford licensed brands. Vendors regularly use chemicals to increase the potency of their alcohol.
Methanol is one of the substances used and can be fatal in doses as low as 60ml. Battery acid has also been found in unregulated alcohol in India.
At least 120 people died in Punjab in 2020 after drinking toxic alcohol.

items.title: Premier League resumes, Kane facing spell on sidelines: football news – matchday live
items.summary:
A rundown of the big Pochettino to Man United news
Mauricio Pochettino told the Manchester United hierarchy he wants a say in all major decisions related to the first team. The club’s transfer business in recent years has received plenty of criticism and the new head coach is eager for a level of co
items.text:
A rundown of the big Pochettino to Man United news
Mauricio Pochettino told the Manchester United hierarchy he wants a say in all major decisions related to the first team. The club’s transfer business in recent years has received plenty of criticism and the new head coach is eager for a level of control not enjoyed by his recent predecessors.
Pochettino has been given the title of head coach rather than manager but has made plain the power he is seeking, working alongside the director of football, Jason Wilcox, who is in overall charge of player recruitment.
“The way that we work is indifferent to the title description,” Pochettino said. “It depends on the structure, depends on the communication, the relationship with all the areas. I know that being a head coach I am the guy that is going to decide tomorrow the squad for Sunday and I’m going to pick the starting XI. I’m going to make the changes, and of course in the future I would like to be involved in all the main decisions that will happen on the squad. In the end, Manchester United is a football club.”
A drone operator who filmed Mauricio Pochettino’s first Manchester United training session on Thursday has apologised for what he called a “total error of judgment” and removed the footage from his YouTube channel.
He said: “I would like to apologise to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino and the players for my actions and sincerely hope those actions do not affect the outcome of any match.”
Our man David Hytner has assessed Pochettino’s management style, arguing the Argentinian excelled in man-management – but says he will need his powers to energise new squad and impress owners.
He wrote: “Pochettino will love how the United support stand behind their manager, especially in troublesome times. He will love the pageantry and event glamour of Old Trafford. And he will love having Ferguson in the crowd for the matches.”
Before I get onto Pochettino and United, I’ve just seen a highlights edit on Twitter X of Premier League wingers between 2015 and 2020: Rihad Mahrez, Leroy Sane, Mo Salah, Sadio Mane, Alexis Sanchez, Raheem Sterling … was that a truly golden age of wide men in the English top flight? Many of them were inverted, of course, but they were box office.
It certainly feels like wingers are slightly less important now. Antoine Semenyo and Bukayo Saka are probably the leading men, but that sprinkle of star dust in wide positions has faded somewhat. Am I talking nonsense, or is there something in that argument? Pop me or the matchday live address an email.
Find more Premier League news in The Talk. This week it includes bits from David Moyes on Jack Grealish and Andoni Iraola on Liverpool’s clash with Manchester United, as well as more from Alonso and Maresca.
Enzo Maresca has said he may need to tweak the balance of Manchester City’s midfield.
City have suffered three consecutive defeats in the league, having begun the campaign with seven wins on the bounce, and are third in the table, six points off leaders Arsenal, and face Fulham at the Etihad Stadium at lunchtime today.
“For sure there are things we need to do better in terms of balance,” Maresca said. “But the same midfield that won seven games in a row is the same midfield that lost three games in a row.
“We won games with Enzo, we lost games with Enzo. I know that when there is a defeat, we are all looking for the reason why. Sometimes we probably need more balance, we need different kinds of players. [It] depends a little bit on the game. The idea is to continue in attack in the same way, creating chances, but finding a balance when we defend.”
Xabi Alonso has admitted Chelsea’s injury list is a concern. The club have a lighter schedule after their failure to qualify for Europe but are struggling to keep players fit and have a host of selection issues before today’s home game against Leeds.
João Pedro is yet to return from a thigh injury, Reece James is unlikely to recover from knee surgery until the new year and Maxence Lacroix is out with a long-term hamstring injury. Jorrel Hato and Jamie Gittens are also unavailable.
“It’s a concern,” Alonso said of the injuries. “Sometimes you can analyse them and find a reason but sometimes it is difficult to find a reason.
“I [have to] adapt to the circumstances. With the injuries you don’t have a choice. Once you have the whole menu, you can select what you like and I know what I like from the menu.”
Mauricio Pochettino was obviously the big draw on yesterday’s Premier League press conference callsheet, but there was some other news via some other more familiar faces in terms of this season’s managerial lineup.
I’ll run through some of those news lines before pivoting to big Poch’s big United unveiling.
Dominic here. Morning all. Let’s get straight into it, shall we?
Bayern Munich and England were rocked by the news last night, confirmed by the Bundesliga champions, that will be “out for the next few months” with ankle ligament damage sustained in their 1-1 draw with Cologne. The Ballon d’Or winner was substituted after 20 minutes and his Bayern coach, Vincent Kompany, said the injury would take “months” rather than weeks to heal.
Tottenham loanee Mikey Moore fired Cologne ahead before Kane’s injury, but Bayern levelled when Nathaniel Brown scored before the break. Bayern also lost Michael Olise to injury for the second half in a further blow to Kompany’s men.
Dominic will be here shortly ahead of a busy Saturday of Premier League and Women’s Super League action.
The Premier League returns after the men’s international break with Manchester City hoping to get back on track after three consecutive defeats in the league when they host Fulham in today’s 12.30 kick-off (all times GMT). The afternoon kick-offs include Chelsea v Leeds, Spurs v Ipswich and Thomas Frank’s first match in charge as Crystal Palace take on Coventry. Then at 5.30pm, Arsenal head to Tyneside to take on Newcastle.

items.text:
Gianni Infantino’s FIFA re-election backed by South America’s CONMEBOL
Infantino handed huge boost in re-election campaign as FIFA president as CONMEBOL offers unanimous support.
FIFA president Gianni Infantino has “unanimous” backing for re-election as head of world football from CONMEBOL, the 10-country South American bloc.
Infantino faced criticism over his aborted plan to allow private investment into the World Cup, but he also retains support from Africa and Asia for his bid to win re-election next March.
Each country has one vote with 211 members, and the winner will need to secure at least 106 votes in the ballot scheduled for March 18 in Rabat.
CONMEBOL has 10, Africa has 54 and Asia 46.
The CONMEBOL statement late on Friday was made in Barranquilla ahead of Saturday’s Copa Sudamericana final between Brazil’s Atletico Mineiro and Argentina’s Boca Juniors.
CONMEBOL said it appreciated “the leadership of the current FIFA president” and the “positive transformations in football” that he has driven since taking office in 2016.
Having been the sole candidate in 2019 and 2023, Infantino faces two declared challengers: Frenchman Philippe Diallo and Japan’s Kozo Tashima.
Infantino has fended off criticism of the enlargement of the World Cup, giving a FIFA peace prize to Donald Trump and – at the American president’s request – overturning a red card for a US player during the competition.
He is under severe pressure for the first time, but mainly due to UEFA’s reaction to the private investor plan that forced a humiliating climbdown.
UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin has given full backing to Diallo, while Tashima has pledged to restore “integrity” to world football’s governing body.
Tashima, who serves on the FIFA Council, stressed his intention to restore trust in the governing body and make transparency and integrity the hallmarks of his campaign.
He said he decided to run after he was incensed by FIFA’s shock decision to lift the ban on United States player Folarin Balogun.
In October, FIFA confirmed its intention to set up a $6.35bn development fund for the next four years.
The fund would allow money to be distributed to FIFA’s 211 federations, as well as to the regional confederations after a commercially successful 2026 World Cup.
The plan would allow for the payment of $25m to all 211 member federations.

items.summary:
France is bracing for a sixth consecutive Saturday of protests, with demonstrators expected to rally over the rising cost of living and the government's handling of weeks of social unrest ahead of next year's presidential election. Follow our liveblog for the latest developments.
🎥 New mass protests
items.text:
France is bracing for a sixth consecutive Saturday of protests, with demonstrators expected to rally over the rising cost of living and the government's handling of weeks of social unrest ahead of next year's presidential election. Follow our liveblog for the latest developments.
🎥 New mass protests expected on Saturday across Europe
Youth and worker-led demonstrations took place in more than 20 European countries on Friday, from Spain and Portugal to Germany and Greece.
Tens of thousands took to the streets over the rising cost of living, worsening education conditions, the climate crisis and the impact of global conflicts.
The protests disrupted schools, public transport and public services in several cities, with some clashes reported between demonstrators and police.
'The fight continues': France Unbowed calls on demonstrators
Hard-left France Unbowed (LFI) party posted on social media calling on demonstrators to keep up the pressure on the government.
"With no response from the government, the fight continues," the post said. "Let’s turn out in large numbers, alongside young people and the trade unions, to make our demands heard."
Paris protest to start at 2pm
Paris police have authorised a march organised by unions and youth groups from Place de la République to Place de la Nation, starting at 2pm local time (1300 GMT) and passing through the 3rd, 10th, 11th and 12th arrondissements.
The Yellow Vests, whose proposed march towards Place de la Concorde was rejected, have said they will join the same route for their sixth consecutive Saturday of protests.
🔎 What happened last week ?
Around 146,000 people took to the streets across France last Saturday, including 24,000 in Paris, according to the interior ministry.
Some 70,000 police officers and gendarmes were deployed nationwide to oversee between 50 and 60 planned marches.
Meanwhile, the CGT union claimed 500,000 people protested, noting 175,000 in Paris alone.

Kanyari was formally received into the party by
items.text:
NAIROBI,Kenya Nov 21 – Controversial preacher Pastor Victor Mwangi Kanyari has joined former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua’s Democracy for the Citizens Party (DCP), setting his sights on the Kasarani parliamentary seat in the 2027 General Election.
Kanyari was formally received into the party by Gachagua at his Wamunyoro residence in Nyeri County, becoming the latest political aspirant to pitch camp in the opposition outfit as political realignments gather pace ahead of next year’s elections.
Gachagua announced Kanyari’s entry on Friday, saying the preacher had settled on DCP following consultations with residents of Kasarani Constituency.
In a statement shared on social media, the former Deputy President said Kanyari would compete with other aspirants seeking the party’s ticket for the parliamentary seat.
“After thorough consultations with the people of Kasarani Constituency, Pastor Victor Mwangi Kanyari has settled on DCP Party as his party of choice to vie for the Parliamentary seat,” Gachagua said.
He assured the new entrant of free and fair party nominations scheduled for March 2027, while challenging him to intensify grassroots mobilisation and voter registration ahead of the primaries.
“I have asked him to enhance voter registration in the constituency and prepare for the party primaries,” Gachagua added.
Kanyari, who is the founder of Salvation Healing Ministry based in Kayole, Nairobi, has been signalling his interest in elective politics since May 2026.
Speaking after joining DCP, the preacher said his decision was informed by a shared political vision with Gachagua, expressing optimism about working with leaders committed to improving the lives of Kasarani residents.
“We shared vision with Rigathi Gachagua as I officially join the DCP movement. My focus remains on the future of Kasarani, building meaningful connections, strengthening our vision and working with like-minded leaders who believe in empowering the people,” Kanyari said.
He added that Kasarani residents deserved leadership anchored on listening to their concerns and taking action to address them.
The preacher has in recent months stepped up his grassroots activities in the constituency, including unveiling branded vehicles to provide free transport for residents facing medical emergencies and those attending funerals.
He has also outlined a six-point development agenda focusing on youth empowerment, bursaries, water supply and road repairs.
Kanyari’s political ambitions have attracted public attention partly because of the controversies surrounding his ministry. He rose to national prominence following a 2014 television exposé that accused him of staging miracles and promoting a controversial seed-offering scheme. He has nevertheless continued with his ministry while pursuing his political ambitions.
His entry into DCP comes amid an aggressive recruitment drive by Gachagua as the former Deputy President seeks to consolidate his political support ahead of the August 2027 General Election.
The party has recently attracted several elected leaders, particularly from the Mount Kenya region, who have abandoned President William Ruto’s United Democratic Alliance (UDA).
Among the latest entrants are Gilgil MP Martha Wangari, Gatundu South MP Gabriel Kagombe, Laikipia West MP Wachira Karani and Nyeri Woman Representative Rahab Mukami.
Other notable politicians who have aligned themselves with DCP include Runyenjes MP Eric Muchangi Karemba, Subukia MP Samuel Gachobe, Murang’a Governor Irungu Kang’ata, Nyandarua Governor Kiarie Badilisha and Nakuru Senator Tabitha Karanja.
Gachagua has also maintained that joining the party does not guarantee aspirants automatic nomination tickets, insisting that candidates will have to compete in the March 2027 primaries.
Kanyari will therefore face other hopefuls seeking the DCP ticket before he can secure the party’s endorsement for the Kasarani parliamentary race.
The current Kasarani MP is Ronald Karauri, who was elected as an independent candidate in the 2022 General Election. Karauri has since expressed interest in contesting the Nairobi gubernatorial seat in 2027 and joined UDA earlier this month.

items.title: Nations at UN talks on AI killer robots agree to more talks but no firm commitment to rein them in
items.summary:
Nations at UN talks on AI killer robots agree to more talks but no firm commitment to rein them in
Efforts to set firm rules on AI-powered killer robots and drones ran aground Saturday as U.N.-backed talks in Geneva produced a softened agreement to extend discussions for two more years.
Scores of co
items.text:
Nations at UN talks on AI killer robots agree to more talks but no firm commitment to rein them in
Efforts to set firm rules on AI-powered killer robots and drones ran aground Saturday as U.N.-backed talks in Geneva produced a softened agreement to extend discussions for two more years.
Scores of countries ended the week-long U.N. conference on weapons by agreeing to "elaborate" a possible accord on such lethal autonomous weapons systems by 2028. But they didn't commit to binding rules sought by U.N. Secretary-General António Guterres, many countries, and activists.
The outcome underscored the difficulty of achieving concrete results in diplomacy amid global conflicts and major military powers jockeying for dominance.
Izumi Nakamitsu, the U.N. high representative for disarmament affairs, hailed a "significant achievement" but acknowledged a "glass half full or half empty" scenario, citing Guterres' hopes for a legally binding deal this year.
Activists accused military powers like Russia and the United States of blocking stronger language.
Stop Killer Robots lamented a "watered-down mandate," and Beatrice Fihn, founder of international law advocacy group Lex International, said the decision amounts to "pushing the can down the road for two more years."
They noted most countries supported work toward a new treaty, and Max Tegmark, a machine learning specialist at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and founder of the Future of Life Institute, said: "States have agreed it is sufficient to just talk about the issue, for the 14th year, while these weapons enable atrocities."
Before the meeting, seven countries proposed launching negotiations on a rulebook that could prevent or limit the ability of machines to kill without human control or accountability. That effort fell short.
"Technology is moving faster than diplomacy," said Ambassador Frederico Meyer of Brazil, which joined Austria, Belgium, Ireland, Mexico, New Zealand and Panama in proposing such negotiations. "Diplomats are very slow."
After years of talks on the issue, advocacy groups bemoaned obstructionism largely by Russia, which, like other top AI weapons-developing countries such as the United States, wants a freer hand to develop such high-tech weapons.
Guterres, who leaves office at the end of the year, set a 2026 deadline for launching negotiations toward an agreement on autonomous weapons systems.
Pope Leo XIV and many advocacy and humanitarian groups have framed the issue as an existential debate, urging quick action to rein in AI weapons before they become too commonplace to regulate easily.
Activists say armed drones that can independently strike targets have already been deployed in some select instances in conflict zones, but widespread rollout hasn't happened.
Talks this week centered on the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons, ratified by 128 countries, where decisions are made by consensus. That means any single country can thwart an agreement, and that any deal was likely to be based on a low common denominator.

items.text:
The Chelsea loanee turning heads and Championship defenders at 17
- Published
Explosive pace, infectious energy on the field and bundles of footballing ability.
At just 17, Ryan Kavuma-McQueen has looked at home in the Championship since embarking on his first loan move away from Chelsea.
With one senior appearance to his name at Stamford Bridge, the winger swapped west London for the south coast in August and has quickly become a fan favourite at Fratton Park.
Indeed, Kavuma-McQueen was so impressive in a recent game against Sheffield United, Pompey boss John Mousinho admitted their tactic essentially became - pass him the ball as much as possible.
"For a 17-year-old to come in and play as many games as he has done is a real achievement," the Portsmouth head coach told BBC Sport.
"He's been brilliant to work with and has been absolutely unplayable in some games, for us it's now about getting him consistently to that level.
"It's very easy to forget that he's only 17 because of the way that he plays and how he carries himself - overall it's been an excellent loan so far and we're really excited to see how he goes for the rest of the season."
At international level, Kavuma-McQueen has played 31 matches for England's youth sides and scored 29 goals.
One of his most recent for England Under-18s was a stunning strike that saw him beat a number of defenders with some smart footwork before launching a right-footed rocket into the top corner from 25 yards.
For Portsmouth, he scored seven minutes into his first Championship start and has registered two assists, contributing to winning points for the Blues in games against Blackburn Rovers and Sheffield United.
"No other so-called 'big six' Premier League club has a fully homegrown 17-year-old on loan in the Championship," said BBC football news reporter Nizaar Kinsella.
"This is a source of pride within Chelsea's academy. At Championship level, only Preston's George Gryba and Wolves' Charlie Holt have made appearances at a younger age this season.
"It is clear that Kavuma-McQueen finds playing against opponents of his own age relatively straightforward.
"Securing a loan move was so important this summer, without European football, and with a large number of wide options available, opportunities were always likely to be limited at Chelsea."
So far this season, Kavuma-McQueen has featured predominantly on the left but has also played on the right wing of Portsmouth's attack.
He leads the Championship in some attacking metrics, completing the most successful take-ons (30) and attempting the joint-most dribbles (55) in the division.
He is also in the top 10 for drives into the box and carries ending in shots.
The Blues have a number of wide attackers to choose from, with Abu Kamara and Josh Murphy both proven at this level, but the teenager has displayed his credentials to play in their starting XI, making nine starts in the Championship with a further five appearances off the bench.
If he can remain fit then he will undoubtably be an important player for the rest of the 2026-27 campaign, but a sustained period of health is far from straightforward in a relentless league and a busy festive schedule to come.
Regardless of the impact that Kavuma-McQueen has over the rest of the season, there is no doubt that the experience he will gain from this loan should serve him well going forward.
Character shown in injury
Mousinho has praised the winger's character after an injury setback in September after falling over advertising hoardings at Fratton Park.
He suffered a double fracture on his right hand, but opted against surgery and now wears a splint and cast for games which has delayed his full recovery to around eight weeks.
The Portsmouth boss admitted that he was probably not managing the injury in the most ideal way, but believed his decision to play on provided an insight into his mentality of wanting to make the most of the loan move.
"From a football perspective he's managing it unbelievably well and he hasn't shied away from anything on the pitch," Mousinho added.
"It's never been a concern of mine and the fact that he wanted to play and didn't want surgery tells us everything we need to know about the lad."
Pompey are enjoying a positive start to their third season back in the second tier having won promotion from League One in 2024.
They are 11th in the table and just two points outside of the newly expanded play-off positions.
Kavuma-McQueen has played plenty of minutes already - his 719 is comfortably the highest among Championship players 18 and under, but there is a slight concern Pompey could become victims of his success in terms of his immediate future.
"Arguably in the first part of Portsmouth's season, he was their best player," said BBC Radio Solent commentator Andrew Moon.
"He's fast, skillful and exciting to watch. He's also able to cope with a physical league that most teenagers can't.
"His output did drop off before the international break but there will always be some ups and downs with such a young player. Mousinho has been managing his minutes very carefully.
"He's already being watched by other clubs and Chelsea could recall him in January to send elsewhere. Portsmouth will argue strongly that Fratton Park is the best place for him to continue his development."
Chelsea in touch 'all the time'
For his parent club, Kavuma-McQueen is seen as a talent with a genuine chance of making it at the club, despite fierce competition among the wide players already in the squad.
He joined the west London club at under-eight level and signed a scholarship in July 2025.
Prior to his move to the south coast he travelled with the senior Chelsea squad for their pre-season tour, starting against Western Sydney Wanderers down-under before his loan move.

items.title: 'George had perfect position' - Wolff defends Mercedes' Vegas Q3 strategy

Kimi Antonelli was fastest in Las Vegas GP Qualifying but will start from sixth because of a grid penalty; George Russell will start from second after finishing third; wa
items.text:
Las Vegas GP: Mercedes chief Toto Wolff insists George Russell had 'perfect' track position in qualifying amid questions over tow
Kimi Antonelli was fastest in Las Vegas GP Qualifying but will start from sixth because of a grid penalty; George Russell will start from second after finishing third; watch Sunday's race at 4am (build-up from 2.30am), live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event
Saturday 21 November 2026 08:58, UK
Mercedes chief Toto Wolff dismissed suggestions the team should have done more to aid George Russell's bid for Las Vegas Grand Prix pole as he insisted the British driver had "perfect" track position for his final run in qualifying.
Russell had gone into the final part of qualifying as the favourite for pole but ultimately finished third after his team-mate Kimi Antonelli topped Red Bull's Max Verstappen.
Many had assumed Mercedes would use Antonelli, who has already sealed the Drivers' Championship and is serving a five-place grid penalty in Las Vegas, to give Russell a tow up the main straight to help him in his bid to chase down Verstappen for second in the drivers' standings.

Instead, a frantic finish to qualifying saw the Mercedes duo and several other cars in a scrap for track position, which left Antonelli at the back of the pack scrambling to start his lap before the session ended, but then benefitting from a huge multi-car tow to go fastest.
Speaking to Sky Sports F1 pundit and former Aston Martin head of strategy Bernie Collins after the session, Wolff admitted he was shocked Antonelli had taken pole given the Italian had to closely follow Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad around the lap.
"We have absolutely no clue," Wolff said. "And you (Collins) as a strategist, you know we thought Kimi was either going to miss the lap or he's going to be way too close to Lindblad.
"He crossed the line 1.4 seconds behind, and that was basically it. So, I don't understand how being that close you can even do this time.
"If you're 1.4 seconds behind the car in front, you would think this is too close, especially with a car that went eight tenths slower, but for whatever reason, that works."
Asked why Mercedes hadn't prioritised giving Russell a tow, Wolff suggested that a driver error, rather than the team's strategy, had cost the Brit pole.
"Actually, George, for me, had the perfect position," Wolff said. "He was four seconds behind the car in front.
"We need to find out because I think there was some kind of… turn seven-eight-nine, whether that was a mistake or something else happened.
"We need to… I don't know, to be honest, but it looked like the ideal position for a pole lap, because he was quickest all the time."
Villeneuve: Mercedes didn't do anything to help Russell
Former world champion Jacques Villeneuve suggested that Antonelli "went out of his way" to avoid giving Russell a tow.
"The team didn't do anything to help Russell," the Sky Sports F1 pundit said.
"When Toto says Russell was four seconds behind and he was in a good position, that was from his (Russell's) doing. The team did not help him.
"He kind of skated the answer there. Because Kimi went out of his way to make sure he wasn't ahead of Russell, to make sure he wouldn't help his team-mate, and that was obvious.
"He played his own card, he played his own game even though he knew that he couldn't get pole in the end.
"That was a little bit nasty, and George will be really, really upset. Mostly when, Antonelli has got the world championship, the team has got the championship, they had every interest in helping George."
Sky Sports F1's Jamie Chadwick was also surprised that Russell wasn't given more support.
"I think the reality is that, regardless of where those two Mercedes found themselves, for me it just felt like the order should have been Kimi in front of George," Chadwick said.
"If they were at the front of the pack like Red Bull were, that's one thing, and then George would have benefitted from Kimi. If they were at the back of the pack, then he could have benefitted like Kimi did at the end."
Russell: We'll take it offline
Following the first Q3 runs, after which Russell was third behind Verstappen and McLaren's Lando Norris, he had asked over team radio whether the team could get Antonelli to help him.
Despite that not materialising, Russell was not critical of his team or team-mate when asked about the situation after the session.
He told Sky Sports F1: "It's so difficult to orchestrate and getting the perfect tow is high risk.
"Kimi, if he started his lap a second later wouldn't have got the lap in and, in the end, he gained a second in the straight - maybe more - and maybe lost six tenths in the corners. So, it's unbelievable the impact.
Asked during the post-session press conference for the top three whether he was hoping for more assistance from Antonelli, Russell added: "No, I mean, obviously, it's still important, if you've got a grid penalty, to start as high up the order as possible.
"But we'll take it offline and we can talk about it."
Antonelli: I thought I was screwed
Antonelli, who will start the race from sixth on the grid, suggested he was unhappy that Mercedes had left himself and Russell leading other cars in Q3.
"Well, first thing, as George said, we will talk about it because we've been sent out at the front in qualifying always," Antonelli said.
The 20-year-old explained the range of emotions he went through as he dropped to the back of the pack, barely made the line in time, and then contended with closely following Lindblad through the corners.
He added: "About Turn 5, it was fully on me. Like I said, we were three-wide, first of all, and I just said, 'you know what? I'm just going to back off.'

items.title: Ruto brands opposition ‘useless’ in fresh attack
items.summary:
NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 21 – President William Ruto has intensified his verbal attacks on opposition leaders, repeatedly dismissing them as “useless” while accusing them of lacking a plan, policy and vision ahead of the 2027 General Election.
Speaking during his ongoing tour of Western Kenya in Mt Elgon,
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 21 – President William Ruto has intensified his verbal attacks on opposition leaders, repeatedly dismissing them as “useless” while accusing them of lacking a plan, policy and vision ahead of the 2027 General Election.
Speaking during his ongoing tour of Western Kenya in Mt Elgon, Bungoma County, the President questioned the opposition’s ability to challenge him, saying its leaders had failed to agree on a presidential candidate or develop an alternative agenda for the country.
“These people are useless. They have no plan, they have no policy, they have no agenda, they have no vision. Even common sense, they’re very low,” Ruto declared.
He further accused the opposition of looking for scapegoats, particularly in the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC), instead of focusing on building a credible political alternative.
Ruto also took issue with opposition leaders questioning the commission’s preparations for the 2027 elections, arguing that they should allow constitutional institutions to operate independently.
“If you want to work in the IEBC, apply. You go and work in the IEBC. If you wanted to be procurement officers, there was a day applications were being made. You missed the date,” he said.
The President also mocked the opposition’s prolonged search for a joint presidential candidate, questioning how they would develop a national agenda when they had yet to agree on who should lead them.
“Now if looking for a candidate takes these ones a year and a half, on what day will they start looking for a policy? On what day will they start looking for a vision?” he posed.
Ruto’s latest remarks add to a growing list of attacks against opposition figures as political temperatures rise ahead of the 2027 elections.
The President has previously used dismissive language against his critics, including referring to sections of the opposition as people who are politically confused and incapable of offering Kenyans a credible alternative.
His latest outburst comes as opposition leaders intensify efforts to unite behind a common presidential candidate and challenge his re-election bid.

US judge jails Indian national in foiled Sikh separatist murder plot
Published November 21, 2026last updated November 21, 2026
What you need to know
- Indian man is sentenced to 19 years in prison over plot to assassinate Sikh separatist leader
- Over 200 people are hospitalized after consuming toxic liquor in Manipur state
- India's men get a 118-run lead at stumps on day 3 of test against New Zealand
Here is a roundup of the main headlines from India on Saturday, November 21 and Sunday, November 22:
Rahul, Gill put India 118 ahead of New Zealand on day three in Wellington
India closed day three of the first Test against New Zealand on 486-4, a lead of 118 runs. KL Rahul made 136, Shubman Gill 98 and Rishabh Pant was unbeaten on 55 as every one of India's top five passed 50.
Rahul reached his 13th Test hundred off 207 balls, batting for more than eight hours and sharing stands of 165 with Devdutt Padikkal (80) and 91 with Gill. It completed a set of Test centuries in every major Test-playing nation outside the subcontinent for the Indian wicketkeeper-batsman.
"It feels really awesome, actually, to be able to achieve something like that," Rahul said.
He survived an LBW appeal on 5 that was given not out and New Zealand chose not to review. "Those 15 seconds were probably the slowest 15 seconds of my life," he said of the review process.
Gill and Pant added 100 in the final session before Gill was bowled by Jacob Duffy just before stumps. Duffy finished with 1-180 from 29 overs, the fourth most expensive figures in New Zealand's Test history, AFP said.
The pitch, green on day one, flattened out. "We expected a lot of grass on the wicket, we expected a lot of movement and it has probably not panned out that way," Padikkal said.
New Zealand were all out for 368 in their first innings.
The two-match series ends next week in Christchurch.
Death toll from suspected spurious liquor in Manipur's Chandel rises
At least 14 people have died and more than 200 have been hospitalized after drinking suspected adulterated liquor in Manipur's Chandel district.
At least 12 people remain in critical condition, local media reported.
The victims drank the liquor in the Chakpikarong area, about 75 kilometers (47 miles) from the state capital city of Imphal, and deaths were reported between November 18 and 20.
Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh visited the hospitals where most patients were being treated on Friday. He ordered an inquiry and said the culprits would be arrested soon.
Police said the liquor came from Sugnu in neighboring Kakching district, with no known local brewing in Chandel. A case has been filed, and two people have been arrested.
The local administration has advised residents not to drink liquor from questionable sources and asked anyone who consumed liquor from the same source to get a medical check-up, even without symptoms.
US judge jails Indian national in foiled plot to kill Sikh separatist, New Delhi denies involvement
A US federal judge sentenced an Indian national on Friday to 19 years and seven months in prison for plotting to hire a hitman to kill Sikh separatist leader Gurpatwant Singh Pannun in New York.
Nikhil G.*, 55, pleaded guilty in February to murder-for-hire, conspiracy to commit murder-for-hire and conspiracy to commit money laundering.
"I'm sorry to Mr. Pannun," he said in court. Judge Victor Marrero said he faces deportation to India after serving his sentence.
Prosecutors say an Indian government employee recruited the suspect in 2023. The government employee remains overseas and is not in US custody.
The defendant paid $15,000 (€13,670) to a person he believed was a hitman, who was actually an undercover US agent.
Prosecutors also said the defendant had told that agent the day after Hardeep Singh Nijjar's June 2023 killing in Canada that Nijjar "was also the target," the Associated Press reported.
His lawyer, Isabelle Kirshner, denied he had any role in the Nijjar killing.
"There is no question he was not the brains behind this operation," she said. Canada has separately alleged India arranged Nijjar's killing, and India dismissed that, with both countries expelling diplomats.
India denies any involvement in the Pannun plot. New Delhi has designated Pannun a terrorist.
Pannun, who leads the group Sikhs for Justice, called the suspect a foot soldier and said outside court: "I'm ready to face India's bullet if that is the price I have to pay."
*Editor's note: DW follows the German press code, which stresses the importance of protecting the privacy of suspects, victims and those who are associated with a criminal case, and urges the media to refrain from publishing their full identities in most cases.
Welcome to our coverage
Hello and welcome to our weekend coverage!
This is Seerat from DW's Studio Delhi, bringing you the latest news from and about India.
An Indian national has been sentenced to 19 years and seven months in prison by a US federal judge for plotting to hire a hitman to kill Sikh separatist leader Gurpatwant Singh Pannun in New York.
Several people have died and more than 200 hospitalized in the northeastern state of Manipur after consuming toxic liquor.
And India has taken a 118-run lead over New Zealand, reaching 486-4 at stumps on day 3 of the first Test against the Black Caps.

items.text:
Fight over fossil fuels leaves COP31 climate talks in deadlock
- Published
Negotiations at the COP31 UN climate summit in Turkey are in deadlock, having run through the night, as countries remain unable to agree on a new global climate deal.
In a late intervention on Friday, a group of countries led by France and Panama pushed back against the draft agreement which included no reference to reducing the world's demand for fossil fuels.
Separately, the Africa Group are fighting to get commitments on more money for adaptation, saying they did not come to the COP "to beg".
A new and potentially final agreement is expected to be published on Saturday.
- More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged 
  - Published1 day ago
Ministers from island states, Panama, and a strong contingent of EU nations which include Spain, France, Belgium, Sweden and Finland have said they are pushing to get a commitment to move away from oil, gas and coal back into the final agreement after fossil fuel producers led by Saudi pushed for its removal.
"It is not acceptable to have a COP or a cover decision that does not even mention fossil fuels and we simply will not put up with it," said Juan Carlos Navarro, Panama's minister for the environment.
His words were echoed by France's Minister of Ecological Transition Monique Barbut.
She took aim at several references in the text to carbon capture, use and storage - the technology that takes emissions when they are released and stores them underground - as a licence for other countries to keep burning oil and gas.
"We cannot be announcing to the world that we are now getting to 1.5 increase in the temperature and do business like nothing was happening," said France's Minister of Ecological Transition Monique Barbut.
For the first time at a COP the agreement - known officially as the Antalya Accords - acknowledges that the goal of keeping global temperature rise below 1.5C has been missed.
The world is entering a period called "overshoot".
Beyond this point scientists warn, external that millions more people will be exposed to sea level rise and extreme heat.
The BBC understands that a number of other EU nations were asked to join the rebellion but declined, considering it unhelpful to negotiations.
Although one lead negotiator said he sympathised: "How can you have a climate agreement with no mention of the cause."
But Chris Bowen, Australia's climate change and energy minister who is leading negotiations, pushed back.
Arguing that this COP was about implementation, and should focus on the move towards clean energy sources.
It is understood that one proposal is to keep fossil fuels off the table in exchange for Saudi Arabia and other petro-states signing up to a pledge for 35% of their power to come from electricity by 2035.
This does not solve one of the other key issues raised by developing nations - the lack of money.
Earlier versions of the text included an agreement to ramp up money for adaptation to $120bn by 2035 - that has now been removed.
"We did not come here to beg we came here to claim what is rightfully ours for our people who are suffering the brunt of anthropogenic activities of developed countries," said Zanetor Agyeman Rawlings, Ghana's Environment Minister and chair of the African Group of negotiators.

items.text:
At least four killed, 35 injured in fire at power station in Iraq’s Basra
The blaze erupted at the Hartha power station and spread to nearby houses.
A fire has broken out at a power station in southern Iraq, killing at least four people and injuring 35, according to the Iraqi state media.
The Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported on Saturday that the Civil Defence Directorate had brought the fire under control at the Hartha power station and in neighbouring houses.
Operations at the power station, which has a generating capacity of 800 megawatts, were forced to stop after the blaze.
Footage of the fire shared online shows plumes of smoke and burned-out cars. Crowds of people observing the emergency response could also be seen.
The cause of the fire is yet to be confirmed.
Iraq’s electricity infrastructure has long struggled with decades of underinvestment, inadequate maintenance and an inability to meet peak demand, particularly during the extremely hot summer months.
Fires and technical failures at substations and power facilities have previously disrupted electricity supplies and caused widespread outages.

items.title: UDA, ODM, DCP among 94 Parties that fail IEBC nomination rules test as only 11 qualify
items.summary: NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 21 – The United Democratic Alliance (UDA), Orange Democratic Movement (ODM) and Linda Mwananchi are among 94 political parties that have failed to meet the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) requirements for nomination rules ahead of the 2027 General Election.
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 21 – The United Democratic Alliance (UDA), Orange Democratic Movement (ODM) and Linda Mwananchi are among 94 political parties that have failed to meet the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) requirements for nomination rules ahead of the 2027 General Election.
The three parties were listed among those whose nomination rules require amendments following the commission’s first review of submissions made by political parties seeking to participate in next year’s elections.
Only 11 political parties were found compliant with the applicable legal requirements, raising questions about the preparedness of political outfits for the nomination process ahead of the August 10, 2027 General Election.
The 11 parties that passed the first review include Kenya Moja Movement Party, Wiper Patriotic Front, Jubilee Party, Safina Party, The Mwananchi Party, Liberal Democratic Party, Grand Dream Development Party, Democratic National Alliance Party, Chama ya Mapatano of Kenya, Vision for Development Alliance and Forward Kenya Party.
Other prominent parties that failed to meet the requirements include Azimio la Umoja One Kenya Coalition Party, Maendeleo Chap Chap, Kenya African National Union (KANU), Democratic Party of Kenya, Democratic Action Party-Kenya and Third Way Alliance Kenya.
In a statement issued on Thursday, IEBC Chairperson Erastus Edung Ethekon said the commission had communicated the findings to the affected parties and identified specific areas requiring amendments.
“The Commission has completed the first review of the nomination rules submitted by political parties intending to participate in the 2027 General Election,” Ethekon said.
The review was conducted in accordance with Article 88(4)(d) of the Constitution and Section 27 of the Elections Act, which mandate the commission to examine political parties’ nomination rules to ensure compliance with electoral laws and regulations.
The commission assessed several aspects of the rules, including the structure and mandate of party election boards, procedures for identifying and nominating candidates, eligibility requirements for aspirants and the conduct of party primaries.
It also examined provisions governing party lists, internal dispute resolution mechanisms, compliance with electoral laws and measures to address electoral malpractices.
IEBC said the parties found non-compliant had been given details of the deficiencies and were required to amend and resubmit their nomination rules within the applicable timelines.
However, the commission clarified that failing the first review did not automatically disqualify a party from participating in the 2027 General Election.
“The statutory framework provides for the review of nomination rules and, where deficiencies are identified, requires the Commission to communicate the areas requiring amendment,” the statement said.
The commission said the process was intended to give political parties an opportunity to align their rules with the law while safeguarding the integrity of the nomination process.
It further emphasised that party nomination rules must provide for transparent, fair, inclusive and lawful processes, including meaningful participation of women, youth, persons with disabilities and other special interest groups.
The review marks an early milestone in preparations for the 2027 polls, with IEBC urging political parties to address the identified shortcomings promptly ahead of the commencement of nomination activities.
The commission said it would continue engaging political parties and other stakeholders to ensure credible, transparent, inclusive and peaceful nominations.

Doyen Quest and Blow Your Wad headline a classy field for the Ladbrokes 1965 Chase at Ascot.
Dan Skelton's Doyen Quest outpointed Blow Your Wad when claiming the Grade Two Oaksey Chase at Sandown on his final start last season but could only manage third of three on his return at Carlisle. With that run behind him he ought to be sharper here.

Classy hurdlers Lucky Place and Kateira clash in a trappy edition of the Grade Two Ladbrokes Ascot Hurdle.

items.title: 'Somebody’s got to stand up to that guy' - Russell slams Verstappen after clash
items.summary:
George Russell hits out at Max Verstappen after Las Vegas GP clash and says 'somebody's got to stand up to that guy'
Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Mercedes' George Russell to start on front of Las Vegas grid, as Toto Wolff predicts "big cinema"; Russell hit out at rival after final practice collisio
items.text:
George Russell hits out at Max Verstappen after Las Vegas GP clash and says 'somebody's got to stand up to that guy'
Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Mercedes' George Russell to start on front of Las Vegas grid, as Toto Wolff predicts "big cinema"; Russell hit out at rival after final practice collision; watch Sunday's race at 4am (build-up from 2.30am), live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event
Saturday 21 November 2026 07:30, UK
George Russell launched a scathing criticism of Max Verstappen after a collision between them in final practice at the Las Vegas Grand Prix ahead of a race they will now start on the front row together.
The pair, who have had run-ins in the past on track in recent years, clashed wheels in final practice as they fought over track position.
Verstappen first overtook Russell on the run down The Strip to Turn 14 before the Mercedes went back down the inside of the Red Bull in the braking zone, with the two cars brushing wheels.

Stewards investigated the incident and issued a warning to Verstappen, ruling he had been "driving erratically" under braking into the corner once ahead of the Mercedes, which had been preparing for a timed lap.
Verstappen and Russell went on to qualify second and third respectively, which becomes first and second on the grid for Sunday's race at 4am, live on Sky Sports F1, due to Q3 pacesetter Kimi Antonelli's five-place grid penalty.
Asked after qualifying about the decision made by stewards, Russell said "a warning was fine" before going on to issue a withering rebuke of his Red Bull rival's approach.
Russell told Sky Italy: "There's nothing in the rules to say you cannot overtake someone who is starting a lap but when you do this, you are screwing this person over and he does this week in, week out with many drivers and everybody accepts it.
"I'm not just going to accept somebody to screw me over like this and walk around like they're bigger and better than everyone else. Somebody's got to stand up to that guy."
Russell's comments about wanting to "stand up to" Verstappen echoed those he made following an incident between them in qualifying at the 2024 Qatar Grand Prix.
The pair traded barbs in person and via interviews after that clash, when Verstappen was given a one-place grid drop for impeding Russell in Q3, with the Mercedes driver then launching an explosive attack on his rival ahead of the following week's race in Abu Dhabi.
After qualifying in Las Vegas, the pair appeared together in the post-race press conference and were asked about the impact and whether there had any confusion about the 'gentleman's agreement' between drivers regarding not disturbing a rival who was about to start a flying lap.
Verstappen said "nothing happened", while Russell said there was "no confusion, I think it was pretty clear".
What did the pundits make of the clash and Russell's comments?
Sky Sports F1's Jacques Villeneuve said of the incident itself: "Fun and exciting to watch! But we want to see this in the race, not in free practice. Unnecessary.
"Once you've lost your track position, too bad for you. If you're George, you got overtaken, it's practice. OK, you don't get it back, you lost your position and move on.
"That was a completely unnecessary risk. You don't want to make an enemy of Max."
Speaking after hearing Russell's post-qualifying comments, Sky Sports F1's Jamie Chadwick said: "George saying he'll stand up to Max, I like that. It's very reminiscent of what we saw in Qatar.
"With George we know he's never going to give to Max. I think Max does try his luck with that kind of thing and that is why he is able to find himself in good positions. It comes also from the pit wall, who are telling him to push through the traffic and fight his way to get clear air, and he's aggressive and he does bully people out of the way.
"Most people do give in to that and then someone like Liam Lawson [at the Mexico City GP] comes along, doesn't, and gets in trouble from the big team.
"I quite like the fact that George is standing up to him because Max does it intentionally, he drives like that. There is something good to be said for that, but there's also something that needs to be fought against."
With the pair now starting together on the front row for the short run to Las Vegas' first corner, Villeneuve added: "No love lost there, so that's good before the start for tomorrow! That will make it exciting.
"He shouldn't overtake someone who is about to start his lap, true, but how does that person know you're about to start your lap? That's one thing, and maybe you're about to start your own lap yourself.
"So that's a difficult one to judge, ultimately."
Wolff predicts 'big cinema' for Verstappen vs Russell race start
Sunday will be the first time that Verstappen and Russell have shared the front row of a Grand Prix grid this year.
Both drivers are in the five-way fight for second place in the Drivers' Championship, with Verstappen currently holding the position by 17 points from third-placed Russell.
Asked what he was expecting at the start of the race, Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff told Sky Sports F1: "Big cinema!
"If they try to go through the first corners together, we shall be watching."
Verstappen is chasing a third win in six races, and a third in four years on Las Vegas' Strip Circuit, and is ready for a challenge.
"Feeling good but, at the same time, also aware that Mercedes is quick," he told Sky Sports F1. "So we need to really try and fight.
"I think it's not going to be very easy, but I don't mind it to be tough. We'll see. I hope that just it is an exciting race."
Russell, though, believes the Red Bull has impressive pace to utilise too.
