items.title: Jeers, injuries and doubters - White's journey back to the top
items.summary:
Jeers, injuries and doubters - White's journey back to the top
- Published
Ben White's crucial goal against world champions Spain on Sunday will not be forgotten by England fans for a long time.
A smart finish to cap a flowing Three Lions move gave Thomas Tuchel's men an almost unbelievable 3-0 lead
items.text:
Jeers, injuries and doubters - White's journey back to the top
- Published
Ben White's crucial goal against world champions Spain on Sunday will not be forgotten by England fans for a long time.
A smart finish to cap a flowing Three Lions move gave Thomas Tuchel's men an almost unbelievable 3-0 lead in Madrid. They hung on - just - meaning White will always be remembered as the player who scored that winner.
But, for White, the moment represented more than just a goal. It signalled a dramatic turnaround in fortunes for his international career - just four years after many thought his England days were over.
The Arsenal defender has had a tough time on the international stage to say the least.
He left the World Cup in 2022 after a disagreement with then assistant manager Steve Holland and made himself unavailable during the rest of Gareth Southgate's time in charge.
Since returning to England duty in March under Tuchel, the 29-year-old has now established himself as arguably England's best right-back - despite facing jeers from sections of his own fans for his decision to leave that camp.
The defender, who initially arrived at Arsenal from Brighton as a centre-back, has had an excellent start to the season, having played a crucial part in the Gunners' first title win for 22 years last time out.
It hasn't been straightforward for him at Arsenal either though. White has had to navigate his own injury problems and at one point when the defender was struggling for fitness, there was talk that the Gunners should look at moving him on.
But White has battled back and even dealt with competition from Jurrien Timber to remain one of Arsenal's key players.
- People don't know full story behind England exile - White 
  - Published9 November
- 60 minutes of perfection, 30 minutes of chaos - an England win for the ages 
  - Published5 days ago
White's England journey
"I think just obviously people don't know the full story, because I never said anything and won't put anyone under the bus", White said before the England win over Spain.
The 29-year-old is keen to put the well-covered departure from the World Cup in Qatar behind him.
After his long absence from playing for England, some supporters did not believe that White should return.
His first appearance at Wembley since that incident in a friendly against Uruguay in March was booed by some supporters, loud enough for Tuchel to be asked about it after the match.
That game in itself was dramatic for White, who scored the opening goal for England before giving away the penalty that saw the Three Lions draw 1-1 with Uruguay.
White, who missed the World Cup with injury, had been expecting the reaction from some fans. But he is used to proving himself and changing the perception around him.
Tuchel was keen to back his player and said in the build-up to the Spain game that he hoped that the chapter was closed on White being booed by his own supporters.
"Obviously a bit tricky and not straightforward, but yes, it's obviously amazing to be here now." White said of his return to England.
White said in that same interview that he would make the same decision again that he did at the World Cup, but it was now time to move on.
His displays show exactly where his mindset is for his country.
He played the final 12 minutes in England's win over Croatia at Wembley before being brought into the starting line-up for England's toughest match of the November international break against Spain.
This new era of England is being dubbed Tuchel 2.0 and White firmly seems to be part of it.
Chelsea defender Reece James is out with injury. He is a big favourite of Tuchel's but cannot be relied upon for every game due to injuries.
White is a key player for the Premier League champions, reliable in defence and a threat in attack while being physically imposing. There is a lot for Tuchel to like.
And with three of his Arsenal team-mates on the pitch as England won the game, and Bukayo Saka to return, White brings the positives of the cohesion of a club side to Tuchel's team.
Arsenal supporters not surprised by his performances
Arsenal supporters will not be surprised by White's excellent performances for England.
Since signing for the Gunners in 2021, not many players can say they have played more of a crucial role in Arsenal's rebirth under Mikel Arteta.
Such is the importance of White, the Gunners attack does not flow as freely when he is not in the side to link up with Martin Odegaard and Saka as he relentlessly produces overlapping runs - a trait he showed when he scored England's third in Madrid.
His team-mates regularly say he is one of the fiercest competitors in training, and he has regularly shown his mentality when it looks as though things are going against him with his club side.
Arsenal signing Timber and a number of injury issues looked to have had White nearing an exit but, such is his determination, each time a challenge comes up he manages to turn it around.
White is a unique character within football, and has even said he doesn't watch the game away from the training ground, but his passion for his profession cannot be doubted.
Gunners fans will know that the level of passion he displayed in Madrid is something he shows every time he is on the pitch for his club side.

items.title: Brighton are rocking the Premier League elite. But can they mount a title tilt?
items.summary:
They lined up in sky‑blue shirts, white shorts. A combined value of £327m. Enzo Fernández, Ayyoub Bouaddi and Elliot Anderson were starting their first match together in Manchester City’s midfield.
But it was a Brighton midfielder who made the game’s first decisive contribution. Yasin Ayari slotted
items.text:
They lined up in sky‑blue shirts, white shorts. A combined value of £327m. Enzo Fernández, Ayyoub Bouaddi and Elliot Anderson were starting their first match together in Manchester City’s midfield.
But it was a Brighton midfielder who made the game’s first decisive contribution. Yasin Ayari slotted the ball home. The away crowd at the Etihad Stadium roared, then watched their team defend relentlessly, securing Brighton’s first league victory away to City.
It was 31 October 2026. There are dangers in reading too much into a single result this early in the season. Teams are still finding their rhythm, new signings bedding in. But this result packed some punch.
If spending decided football matches, Brighton & Hove Albion should not be competing with, let alone beating, Manchester City, who sign established stars for astronomical fees and wages. Erling Haaland is paid £525,000 a week.
According to an independent commission, to circumvent the Premier League’s spending limits, which restrict a club’s losses, City artificially inflated their commercial revenues by £830m between 2009 and 2018. Brighton, by contrast, tend to buy potential, scouring the market for undervalued talent, often in less prominent leagues. After developing them and benefiting from their performances, the club sell them for profits.
They paid just £3.5m for Ayari, offering him about £10,000 a week, and paired him in midfield with Chema Andrés and Pascal Gross, signed for a combined fee of less than £25m.
The most remarkable thing about Brighton’s win was that it wasn’t really a shock. In September, they dismantled Arsenal, the Premier League champions and favourites for the title. As they prepare for Sunday’s match at Hull, they are second in the league, sandwiched between Arsenal and City, and have scored more goals than anyone else in the division. How, then, do Brighton excel on the pitch without haemorrhaging money? And is there a ceiling to what they can achieve?
On a crisp late October morning, I drove to Brighton in search of answers. Deep inside the Amex, the club’s stadium, I met Paul Barber, Brighton’s CEO, a cheerful man who speaks with the calmness of someone with nowhere else to be.
“Being the size of club that we are, we had to find a way of being competitive that was probably different to any of the other bigger clubs that we were aiming to compete with,” Barber said, “because their revenues are always going to be higher: bigger stadiums, more established sponsorship models, bigger stars, bigger brands.”
Hours before Brighton beat City, Chelsea had beaten Manchester United. In their respective midfields were Moisés Caicedo and Carlos Baleba, whom Brighton had signed for a combined fee of less than £30m and sold for about £180m. “It’s those trading profits that are effectively the core of the Brighton model,” Barber explained.
Most clubs recruit and develop talent, I pointed out, but few do it better than Brighton. Who, outside Ecuador, had heard of Caicedo before he signed for Brighton in 2021? Two years later, the world’s biggest clubs were competing for his signature. The same can be said of dozens of others, among them Marc Cucurella and Alexis Mac Allister. One diamond exits, another enters. Caicedo replaced Yves Bissouma in central midfield. Baleba replaced Caicedo. The same applies to the dugout. Before joining Brighton, Fabian Hürzeler was coaching St Pauli in Germany; before him, Roberto De Zerbi had been at Shakhtar Donetsk.
Barber grinned. “There’s a myth that we have this secret supply of players,” he said. The explanation is Jamestown Analytics, a sports analytics company founded by the club’s owner, Tony Bloom, as an offshoot of Starlizard, the gambling consultancy he established in 2006. Just as Starlizard uses proprietary modelling to identify mispriced odds in betting markets, Jamestown uses algorithms to identify underdeveloped football talents. “They’re all out there,” Barber said. “The data just enables Brighton to home in on them faster and earlier.”
When I asked for more detail about how the system works, Barber fiddled with his watch. Jamestown tracks a vast number of performance indicators for every player competing in professional football, many of which aren’t captured by other data providers. “Every action that players are taking on a football pitch is being looked at, measured and codified in some way,” he said.
When the club identify a position to strengthen, they draw up a list of attributes for the ideal player. Some are universal to the position: a centre-back generally needs to be tall. Others depend on the specific coach and their style of football.
Later, when I spoke to Hürzeler, the head coach, he explained that the data had to reflect the specific demands of his playing system. “A player needs to have some basic things that fit our style of play, so if a player doesn’t want to have the ball then it’s difficult to play in our team. If a player doesn’t want to press high then it’s difficult to play in our team. These are just two examples.”
One reason Brighton recruited Luka Vuskovic in July 2026 was because Hürzeler wanted a mobile centre-back. Reflecting on the City match, Barber recalled seeing Vuskovic pushing “so far forward that you’d have thought he was a right midfielder”. It was the sort of mobility Hürzeler’s system demanded, and Jamestown had identified.
‘The numbers have to be right’
Before Brighton’s victory over City, I met Mike Cave, the club’s sporting director, at the Lowry hotel in Manchester. A few of the Brighton players wandered around in club tracksuits. Cave wore a suit and tie and his hair was slicked back. He was telling me it was a big day without saying it.
Brighton’s recruitment advantage lies not simply in the quality and quantity of the data at their disposal, he said, but in their ability to interpret it and trust what it tells them. “You could have the best data in the world but if you’re not accustomed to using it, and if you’re not clear a

items.title: Van Gerwen 'preparing for the worst' as he faces Sykes in Grand Slam quarters
items.summary:
Michael van Gerwen 'preparing for the worst' as he faces Tom Sykes in Grand Slam of Darts quarter-finals
Michael van Gerwen expected to face Luke Humphries in the quarter-finals but will now take on Tom Sykes and knows he needs to be prepared for a real contest; you can watch the Grand Slam of Darts
items.text:
Michael van Gerwen 'preparing for the worst' as he faces Tom Sykes in Grand Slam of Darts quarter-finals
Michael van Gerwen expected to face Luke Humphries in the quarter-finals but will now take on Tom Sykes and knows he needs to be prepared for a real contest; you can watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports until November 22
Friday 20 November 2026 18:41, UK
Michael van Gerwen is through to his first premier ranking quarter-final in over a year but he is up against an opponent he probably did not expect.
Van Gerwen put in a stellar display in a battle of two darting juggernauts when he defeated James Wade 10-8 to make it through to the final eight at the Grand Slam of Darts.
The 'Green Machine' battled hard against everything Wade threw at him and, with a late surge and some superb finishing, he got the victory over the line.
Now, he is preparing for a quarter-final in Wolverhampton but instead of the predicted clash with world No 2 Luke Humphries, he is up against the 72nd-ranked player on the Tour in Tom Sykes.
Sykes pulled off a stunning final-leg victory over Humphries to make the quarter-finals on his debut at the major.
The Dutchman was impressed with what he saw from the 'Castleford Tiger' and knows that if he can beat Humphries, then he needs to expect the unexpected.
"Tom did really well against Luke. I didn't expect that, I think no one expected that, because this is the first time he's played such a long format on such a big TV appearance," he said.
"A win is a win and moving forward I think this gives me a lot of confidence.
"I have to face Tom who had a fantastic game against Luke, 100 average, loads of 180s, so I need to make sure I am prepared for anything.
"He is a fantastic player; he's been doing really well lately on the Tour, but now he has to deal with the fact that he's going to be first to 16. He's never been in this situation, so it will be new for him as well.
"But don't get me wrong, if you can beat Luke, he can beat anyone, so I need to make sure I prepare myself for the worst."
Van Gerwen has had well-documented ups and downs in his darting career over the last two years but has had glimpses of the levels everyone knows he can reach, his massive win against Wade the latest.
He admitted that the victory, and the manner of it, helped him overcome some demons about his own game and he is now looking to turn that into consistency.
"Yes, I did (overcome some demons). Of course, when you're not doing what you are capable of, it can be a really frustrating game," Van Gerwen added.
"But then to finally do it and also in the way how I did it, I think that gives me energy also towards the next game.
"I always believe in my own ability, otherwise I wouldn't be here. If I think I can't believe in myself anymore, that's the day I have to stop playing darts.
"But that day is not there, and it won't be there in the next few years, it is as simple as that.
"My consistency is starting to get better, my belief in my own ability starts to get better, if you also look towards the Pro Tours and everything, my game starts to get somewhere, and that's what you want, that's where you put the work in and the effort.
"That is how darts is, and darts can be a really cruel game, but at the moment I am still in so that's a good thing."

items.title: Antonelli fastest but Verstappen on pole after dramatic Las Vegas qualifying
items.summary:
Las Vegas GP: Kimi Antonelli fastest but Max Verstappen on pole from George Russell after dramatic qualifying
Kimi Antonelli was quickest in qualifying but a five-place grid penalty for a new engine means Max Verstappen will be on pole from George Russell for the Las Vegas Grand Prix; watch Sunday's
items.text:
Las Vegas GP: Kimi Antonelli fastest but Max Verstappen on pole from George Russell after dramatic qualifying
Kimi Antonelli was quickest in qualifying but a five-place grid penalty for a new engine means Max Verstappen will be on pole from George Russell for the Las Vegas Grand Prix; watch Sunday's race at 4am (build-up from 2.30am), live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event
Saturday 21 November 2026 05:30, UK
Kimi Antonelli was fastest in qualifying for the Las Vegas Grand Prix but a five-place grid penalty means Max Verstappen will start on pole position from George Russell.
New Formula 1 world champion Antonelli will start sixth due to a grid penalty for exceeding his internal combustion engine allocation and surprisingly went fastest in a hectic end to Q3.
The Mercedes driver only just crossed the line in time to start a final flying lap and was helped by a huge slipstream from the Racing Bulls throughout the lap to beat Verstappen by 0.258s.
- Las Vegas GP: UK schedule and how to watch on Sky Sports

Russell was 0.331s behind Antonelli but the Verstappen-Russell front row cannot be missed when the lights go out at 4am UK time on Sunday (build-up from 2.30am), live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event, after the pair made contact in final practice.
Neither driver was penalised as Verstappen was given a warning for driving erratically when trying to stop Russell from gaining track position in final practice earlier on Saturday.
McLaren's Lando Norris will start third with Red Bull's Isack Hadjar in fourth and Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad will start in fifth, his highest career grid position.
Oscar Piastri qualified seventh but the McLaren driver has a 10-place grid penalty for exceeding his engine allocation, so will start 17th, so Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson will start seventh instead.
Alpine's Pierre Gasly and Franco Colapinto had great pace throughout qualifying but were caught up in the traffic chaos in Q3 on the out laps, so only qualified ninth and 10th.
Ferrari had a disaster as they struggled in the cold conditions and on the long straights, so both Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton were knocked out in Q2
It is the first time no Ferrari driver has reached Q3 since the 2024 Canadian Grand Prix and Hamilton was shocked both he and Leclerc did not get through.
Due to the grid penalty for Piastri, Leclerc will start 10th and Hamilton in 11th for Sunday's race.

items.title: Cummins to remain captain after 'unanimous support' from Cricket Australia
items.summary:
Pat Cummins to remain Australia captain, given 'unanimous support' by cricket board amid 'Sandpapergate' fallout
Pat Cummins confirms he will "100 per cent support" forum Cricket Australia has set up following Usman Khawaja's 'Sandpapergate' allegations; CA chair David Boon rejects notion Cummins' i
items.text:
Pat Cummins to remain Australia captain, given 'unanimous support' by cricket board amid 'Sandpapergate' fallout
Pat Cummins confirms he will "100 per cent support" forum Cricket Australia has set up following Usman Khawaja's 'Sandpapergate' allegations; CA chair David Boon rejects notion Cummins' integrity has been "compromised" amid varying accounts from players of 2018 ball-tampering scandal
Saturday 21 November 2026 05:28, UK
Pat Cummins will remain as Test and ODI captain after being given "unanimous support" by Cricket Australia, with the skipper confirming he will take part in the independent forum launched following Usman Khawaja's 'Sandpapergate' allegations.
Cummins' position had been under increasing scrutiny since Cameron Bancroft wrote a detail-filled account of the scandal in the West Australian newspaper, backing up Khawaja's claims that every member of the 2018 side was aware of the sandpaper plot.
Bancroft - the player caught on camera trying to alter the condition of the ball in South Africa eight years ago - said he was stirred to break his silence by Cummins' vehement denials of knowledge of the scheme in a press conference last week.
- Pat Cummins faces fresh scrutiny over Sandpapergate claims
- Sandpapergate: News and reaction to ball-tampering scandal
- Listen to latest episode of the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast
After Cricket Australia chair David Boon and CEO Todd Greenberg met Cummins in Sydney on Friday, a statement released on Saturday read: "In the light of the ongoing speculation surrounding the Australian men's team tour of South Africa in 2018, the CA board met to ensure measures are in place to protect the integrity of Australian Cricket and the welfare of all concerned.
"As part of this meeting, the board resolved to express its unanimous support for Pat Cummins as captain given ongoing speculation about his position."
Cummins prepared for 'difficult conversations' in forum
Cummins, who is set to lead Australia in a four-Test series at home to New Zealand from December 9, with the first match in Bancroft's native Perth, said: "Being Australian captain carries with it an awesome responsibility.
"I have and never will take that lightly.
"David (Boon) and Todd (Greenberg) have a very tough job navigating cricket through all of this and I commend them for reaching out to me and to many of the players and staff from 2018.
"I support the forum 100 per cent. I will be there. All of the players and staff I have spoken with are very keen to have their say. There will be a lot of difficult conversations but that is what's needed.
"Otherwise, from this point, captaining the Australian team in Perth will be my focus and priority."
Boon: Cummins' integrity has not been compromised
Boon added: "We've expressed our support to Pat and our concern for everyone impacted by the events of the 2018 tour of South Africa.
"We have learned from that experience and are proud of the team and the culture Pat and other leaders in the team have fostered over the past eight years and unequivocally reject any implication that Pat's integrity has been compromised.
"We are absolutely determined to steward Australian cricket through this very difficult time with diligence and patience and to listen and learn.
"That's what the independent forum we announced this week is about and the board encourages all players and support staff to tell and discuss their stories there.
"We will be publishing the terms of reference in due course."

"For me, it's not about me. We've earned ourselves to get to the playoffs here and my job is to be
items.text:
BJ Callaghan said he remains fully focused on leading Nashville SC through the Major League Soccer playoffs, amid links to replacing Mauricio Pochettino as United States men's national team head coach.
"For me, it's not about me. We've earned ourselves to get to the playoffs here and my job is to be a leader of this team and one of the leaders in this club," Callaghan told reporters on Friday.
- Pochettino: 'Massive' pressure with USMNT makes me better coach for Man United
- Ex-U.S. coach Arena: Federation doesn't 'have a clue' how to replace Poch
- MLS playoff Round 1 predictions: Who will move on to the conference semifinals?
"My focus is 100% on the players, the staff, the fans and overall this soccer club to make sure what happened in the regular season, we can make it an extension into the playoffs because we have more things to achieve here."
Pochettino departed his role as U.S. coach this week to become Manchester United's new coach. U.S. Soccer announced under-23 coach Steve Cherundolo will lead the team during the December international camp while the search for Pochettino's replacement is underway.
Callaghan previously served as an assistant to then-USMNT coach Gregg Berhalter before taking over interim charge in 2023. He led the group to the Concacaf Nations League title and reached the semifinals of the Gold Cup later that year before Berhalter was re-appointed.
Callaghan joined Nashville in 2024 and turned the team into a trophy-winning side.
Nashville lifted the U.S. Open Cup in 2025, when defeating Austin FC, and earned the 2026 MLS Supporters' Shield. Callaghan also inspired the Eastern Conference team to break the league's record for most points in a single season, with 77 points in 34 games, shattering Inter Miami's previous tally.
Nashville will now face FC Cincinnati in the best-of-three round one playoff series starting on Sunday.
Former Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Manchester City coach Pep Guardiola has been the biggest name linked to replacing Pochettino. Before his departure following a Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal win over Haiti on Tuesday, Pochettino encouraged anyone interested to take the job.
"It's the perfect moment to arrive to the [U.S. Soccer] Federation," Pochettino told reporters at a roundtable Monday. "Everything is in the right direction. I think, of course, take [it]. Take it because he's going to find really good people, good players. The player can fit for his style; the National Training Center that wasn't [there] before."

items.title: LA Galaxy pass on permanent move, send Lozano back to San Diego FC
items.summary:
LA Galaxy announced the club will not exercise the option to permanently acquire Hirving "Chucky" Lozano after his loan spell, as the forward returns to San Diego FC ahead of the 2027 sprint season.
"Hirving Lozano has completed his loan with the Galaxy and returned to his parent club, San Diego FC,
items.text:
LA Galaxy announced the club will not exercise the option to permanently acquire Hirving "Chucky" Lozano after his loan spell, as the forward returns to San Diego FC ahead of the 2027 sprint season.
"Hirving Lozano has completed his loan with the Galaxy and returned to his parent club, San Diego FC," the Galaxy announced in a press release when it made its 2026 roster decisions public.
The Galaxy signed Lozano on loan as a Designated Player in August through December 2026, with a permanent trade option included in the contract. He played 10 matches for the club, recording two goals and one assist, before the Galaxy made the decision to end his time with the club.
Lozano originally signed with San Diego FC in June 2025 while still under contract with PSV Eindhoven, months ahead of the expansion team's MLS debut. He finally joined the club in January, playing 27 matches in their inaugural season before conflict led him to the sidelines.
The Mexican forward was first left off the roster for San Diego FC's first-ever MLS playoff match following a report of a locker room altercation. Head coach Mikey Varas hinted that Lozano could be back with the team soon.
Lozano publicly apologized for his reaction inside the locker room before tensions escalated.
By January 2026, sporting director Tyler Heaps and Varas confirmed Lozano would no longer be taken into consideration.
"Our stance remains the same," sporting director Tyler Heaps told ESPN ahead of the team's 2026 season opener. "Hirving is not and will not be part of our sporting plans heading into this year."
Lozano trained independently for months before eventually signing with the Galaxy in August. It remains unclear what his role with San Diego will be in 2027 following his return from the loan spell.
The Galaxy also announced that veteran defender Maya Yoshida will depart after captaining the club for three and a half seasons. The Japan international made 117 appearances across all competitions and was a cornerstone of the squad that captured the club's sixth MLS Cup title in 2024.

items.title: ANC fights to keep control of South Africa's key cities after election setback
items.summary:
ANC fights to keep control of South Africa's key cities after election setback
- Published
The party that has dominated South Africa for more than 30 years is in a race against time to secure power-sharing deals in most of the country's cities after a massive drop in its support in this month's loca
items.text:
ANC fights to keep control of South Africa's key cities after election setback
- Published
The party that has dominated South Africa for more than 30 years is in a race against time to secure power-sharing deals in most of the country's cities after a massive drop in its support in this month's local elections.
The African National Congress (ANC) suffered its worst result since it came to power in 1994 when South Africa transitioned from the racist apartheid system to democracy.
It won a majority in just one of the country's nine provinces, Limpopo, down from six in the last elections. It won the most votes in just two of the country's eight cities, compared with six in 2021.
At the national level, the ANC is sharing power with its long-time rival, the Democratic Alliance (DA), but while there is still no official announcement, it appears that ANC party officials do not want to replicate this at the local level.
Parties have until 27 November to negotiate and form local governments.
What happened in the local election?
While the ANC saw a massive decline in its support, it still got more votes than any other party, 31%, down from the 46% in the last local election.
But in the country's economic powerhouse, Gauteng province, which includes Johannesburg and Pretoria, the picture is different. The pro-business DA got the most votes in both cities, as well as the province's other main region, Ekurhuleni.
Nationally, the party got 25% of the vote, up from 22% five years ago.
It also retained its majority in its power base of Cape Town, and got the most votes in Nelson Mandela Bay, where Gqeberha (Port Elizabeth) is located.
The left-leaning uMkhonto weSizwe (MK) Party, led by former President Jacob Zuma, came third, with 10% of the vote. This is a repeat of its performance in the 2024 national election, when it came in third and became the official opposition after the DA joined the coalition government.
It emerged as the biggest party in KwaZulu-Natal province, which includes the port city of Durban, securing 34% of the vote. However, this leaves it reliant on agreeing a coalition with other parties.
The only party to secure an overall majority in a city was the DA in Cape Town.
Why is the ANC apparently choosing smaller parties over the DA?
The DA and ANC have had an uneasy alliance since they entered a coalition, along with eight other political parties, in 2024.
The two, long-standing rivals due to their opposing policies, were forced into an agreement after the ANC lost its parliamentary majority for the first time since the end of apartheid. This became known as the Government of National Unity (GNU).
Despite this, the two parties have continued to disagree on key issues, and both sides have threatened to rip up their power-sharing deal.
Ahead of the local elections, analysts predicted that the two parties could team up at municipal level, mirroring the national arrangement.
The ANC seems to have rejected this, with state broadcaster SABC reporting that most of the party's top leaders see an agreement with the DA as a last resort.
Instead, the party has been courting smaller parties to try and form councils in South Africa's cities.
In Gauteng, numerous reports point to an arrangement between the party and the anti-immigrant ActionSA, which emerged as the third largest party in the province with 17%, leaving it as a potential kingmaker.
The DA has also been trying to reach arrangements with smaller parties, and the ANC, but looks set to assume the opposition benches at least in Gauteng.
ActionSA is unlikely to work with the DA as they cannot agree on the mayoral candidates in Johannesburg and Pretoria.
Does this signal a breakdown in the relationship between the ANC and DA nationally?
It's too early to tell. Neither the ANC nor DA have spoken publicly about the future of their arrangement on a national level amid the ongoing coalition talks but the ANC's reluctance to partner with the DA in key cities points to continued strain between the two.
While the GNU has remained intact since it was formed in 2024, there have been those in the ANC who have been angered by what they view as the DA's dual role as opposition and partner in the coalition government and have pushed for the arrangement to end.
A party insider told the Daily Maverick on Sunday that a nationwide agreement to work with the DA at municipal level "was overwhelmingly rejected" at a meeting held by ANC members.
While some experts predict that the DA may have to consider its position in the coalition government given the ANC's stance, political analyst Andre Duvenhage told the BBC there was a possibility that "a lot of asymmetrical coalitions" could emerge - parties working together in one area and being in opposition elsewhere.
Another political analyst, Sandile Swana, said that any party wanting to leave the GNU over the failure to secure deals locally would be "[shooting] yourself in the foot".
Would coalition governments improve services?
This is what voters want.
The decline in the ANC's support was seen as being mainly due to high levels of corruption and a loss of confidence in its ability to provide basic services, such as electricity, water and rubbish collection.
While some attribute the increase backing for the DA to its record of competent management in municipalities under its control, some have accused it of neglecting poorer areas and townships.
But the experience of coalition governments over the past 10 years does not inspire much confidence that things will improve.
Half of the country's cities have been governed through power-sharing agreements since 2016 and these types of arrangements have often been viewed as unstable and chaotic.
As agreements collapse and new ones are forged, the delivery of basic services has often been affected.
This has been particularly evident in Gauteng, where governance in all three cities has come under scrutiny in recent years partly because of unstable governments.

items.text:
Cost of Man Utd hiring and firing managers nears £100m
- Published
Manchester United borrowed another £10m three days after confirming Mauricio Pochettino as their new head coach.
In an extended Stock Market filing to go with their first-quarter financial results that were released on Thursday, United said they would be liable to pay £7.5m in compensation to US Soccer to hire the Argentine.
United announced Pochettino had agreed a two-and-a-half-year deal on 13 November. They borrowed £10m on 16 November.
The loan is one of three confirmed after the 30 September first-quarter reporting date, which takes the overall amount owed on their rolling credit limit to £240m.
The amount paid to release Pochettino from his USA deal takes the sums paid hiring and firing managers since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013 to £95m. However, that figure is likely to top £100m once the cost of hiring Pochettino's staff and sacking Michael Carrick is added.
Carrick was sacked last week with the club in the relegation zone and enduring their worst start to a season in 40 years. The former midfielder only signed a two-year contract in the summer after a successful six-month spell in caretaker charge last season.
Pochettino is the ninth full-time manager to be appointed since Ferguson, including Ralf Rangnick in November 2021. United have changed their manager in the middle of the last three campaigns.
The club also confirmed they had spent £5.7m to either acquire or extend registrations of "certain players and members of coaching staff".
The filing also revealed they owe £417m in outstanding transfer fees, £181m of which is due after one year. United said on Thursday their substantial $750m debt was £577.4m when converted to sterling on 30 September.

items.title: Bayern Munich confirm Harry Kane ‘out for next few months’ with ankle injury
items.summary:
Bayern Munich have confirmed Harry Kane will be “out for the next few months” with ankle ligament damage sustained in their 1-1 draw with Cologne on Friday.
Kane was substituted after 20 minutes of the Bundesliga game, having been left limping after a challenge from the Cologne defender Joël Schmied
items.text:
Bayern Munich have confirmed Harry Kane will be “out for the next few months” with ankle ligament damage sustained in their 1-1 draw with Cologne on Friday.
Kane was substituted after 20 minutes of the Bundesliga game, having been left limping after a challenge from the Cologne defender Joël Schmied. The Ballon d’Or winner was substituted with the returning Bayern coach, Vincent Kompany, saying afterwards that the injury would take “months” rather than weeks to heal.
A club statement on X said: “Harry Kane suffered a tear of the syndesmosis ligament in his left ankle in Bayern Munich’s Bundesliga home match against Köln on Friday evening. This was confirmed by an examination by Bayern Munich’s medical department. The 33-year-old will therefore be out for the next few months.”
The Tottenham loanee Mikey Moore fired the visitors ahead before Kane’s injury, but Bayern levelled things up when Nathaniel Brown scored before the break. Bayern also lost Michael Olise to injury for the second half, and Said El Mala missed an excellent late chance to earn Cologne’s first win at Bayern since 2009.
The 33-year-old may face a race to be fit for the Nations League quarter-finals, with the first leg in Norway taking place on 27 March – just over four months away. The Bayern sporting director, Max Eberl, said on Friday that club doctors were “currently discussing whether or not to recommend surgery” for Kane’s injury.
Part of Kane’s recovery period will come during the Bundesliga’s winter break from 20 December to 8 January. He will, however, miss Champions League games away to Lille next week and at home to Slavia Prague next month, as well as the January trip to Manchester United and the league phase finale at home to Real Betis.
Kane’s setback adds to an extensive Bayern injury list, with Michael Olise also going off during Friday’s game with a foot contusion. Luis Díaz, Serge Gnabry, Alphonso Davies, Ismael Saibari and Manuel Neuer were already unavailable, leaving Kompany short of options for a busy month of fixtures.
Kompany returned from his own month-long absence for Friday’s game with his arm in a sling, having dislocated his shoulder when he collapsed on a training pitch in October. The Belgian was taken to hospital for meningeal irritation treatment after his collapse, and has been recovering at home.
Cologne took a surprise lead with 12 minutes gone as Moore started and finished an excellent break. The teenage winger pounced on a mislaid Olise pass and drove forward, finding Linton Maina who laid off for El Mala, whose no-look backheel pass allowed Moore to round keeper Jonas Urbig before sliding the ball home.
Kane was then brought down in the Cologne box from behind by defender Schmied, who got the ball first but clattered into Kane’s left leg in his follow-through. Kane’s penalty appeals were waved away, but he was left visibly limping and received treatment on his ankle before being replaced by Tom Bischof on the 20-minute mark.
The hosts levelled 17 minutes later as full-back Brown sliced a low shot into the bottom-right corner, but suffered another blow just before the break when Olise went down. The France star did not return to the field for the second half, and was seen leaving the stadium shortly after on crutches – but it appears unlikely he will miss a significant amount of time.
Just before the hour mark, El Mala and Maina forced a spectacular double save from Urbig just before the hour mark. Recent Germany call-up El Mala then had a golden chance to put Cologne in front with eight minutes to go when one-on-one with Urbig – but he cut his close-range shot inches wide of the post.
Now a point behind Bayern, chasers Borussia Dortmund can move into outright first in the table if they win at bottom club Mönchengladbach on Saturday. Freiburg can also move level on points with Bayern if they can defeat promoted Elversberg.
Kane earlier this month signed a new deal with the Bundesliga giants until June 2029 which is reportedly worth in excess of £400,000 a week, making him the highest-paid player in Europe before bonuses.
Since arriving from Tottenham three years ago, Kane has bagged an incredible 156 goals in 163 appearances, helping Bayern win a league and cup double last season.

The seven-time Super Bowl winner has recently divested his stake in Championship club Birmingham City, which he bought into following Tom W
items.text:
NFL great Brady could buy Chelsea stake
- Published
American football great Tom Brady is looking to invest in Chelsea through ownership group Clearlake Capital.
The seven-time Super Bowl winner has recently divested his stake in Championship club Birmingham City, which he bought into following Tom Wagner's Knighthead Capital takeover in 2023.
It now appears he could move into Chelsea, where he has a positive relationship with influential co-owner Behdad Eghbali, having been a star guest at the after-party following the club's Club World Cup triumph in 2025.
Brady would have no voting rights or control at Chelsea, although the ownership group could look to appoint him to the board if it suited all parties.
The move is not said to be linked to Todd Boehly and Mark Walter's £950m sale of their stakes to Clearlake Capital, which must be completed by the end of the year.
Meanwhile, Swiss billionaire Hansjorg Wyss remains a significant minority stakeholder at Stamford Bridge.
The investment is also not part of a funding round, according to senior sources, and is not intended to dilute Clearlake Capital's control.
However, other interested parties are said to have approached them about investing since Boehly and Walter agreed a deal to leave.
Former quarterback Brady, a three-time NFL most valuable player, retired in February 2023 after 23 seasons in the NFL, having won six Super Bowl rings with the New England Patriots and one with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
Following the end of his playing career he acquired a stake in the Las Vegas Raiders, while also becoming part of the ownership group of the WNBA's Las Vegas Aces.
On top of that, Brady's commitments include him being a lead NFL analyst for Fox Sports.

items.summary:
Lauren Price makes boxing history for Wales with first undisputed championship win as she shuts out Michaela Kotaskova
Lauren Price beat Michaela Kotaskova at the Utilita Arena in Cardiff to become the undisputed welterweight world champion; winning a unanimous decision saw Price add the WBO title t
items.text:
Lauren Price makes boxing history for Wales with first undisputed championship win as she shuts out Michaela Kotaskova
Lauren Price beat Michaela Kotaskova at the Utilita Arena in Cardiff to become the undisputed welterweight world champion; winning a unanimous decision saw Price add the WBO title to the WBA, WBC and IBF belts she already had; Price is Wales' first undisputed champion in the four-belt era
Friday 20 November 2026 23:28, UK
Lauren Price made history for Welsh boxing when she beat Michaela Kotaskova to become the undisputed welterweight world champion.
With a unanimous decision victory over Kotaskova at the Utilita Arena, a shutout 100-90 for all three judges, Price added the vacant WBO 147lbs title to the IBF, WBC and WBA belts.
An Olympic gold medallist in 2021, Price is the first Welsh boxer to become an undisputed world champion in the four-belt era.
The first female British champion too, the skilful southpaw started busily and with intent. She planted stiff left crosses through the middle, that back hand arrowing between Kotaskova's gloves and catching her chin.
Price stamped her authority on the fight, teeing off with flurries. Firm right hooks shook Kotaskova.
Price moved backwards and off to the sides, leaving the tall Kotaskova striding after her. When the Czech planted her feet to swing wildly, Price beat her to the punch with rapid, accurate salvoes.
Kotaskova absorbed hits and marched forward. But her grim efforts yielded scant result and in the fifth round Kotaskova was badly cut by her left eye after an accidental head clash.
She didn't let that dissuade her but Price continued to dictate the action. In the sixth round the Welsh star dug her feet into the canvas to uncork a hard three-punch combination.
In the next round Price hammered the body once more and brought a right hook back up to the head. She moved away well, as Kotaskova ran out of ideas.
A swiping left hook from Price knocked Kotaskova away. Price ground in draining body shots.
Kotaskova desperately sought to apply pressure in the 10th and final round, but she could not pin the Welsh star down, who picked her off and raised her arms to celebrate in the final seconds before the bell to end it.
Kotaskova had made her work but the decision was still a formality, and a reflection of Price's dominance.
"I just feel so lucky to be Welsh," Price told the BBC. "This goes out to you lot, thank you, it means the world.
"Nothing really tops that. Winning the Olympic gold medal, that's a dream from the age of eight.
"As a professional everyone's dream is to become undisputed and I can honestly say I've ticked every accolade there is in boxing. I'm not finished. I've got many years left in me.
"It's all about the big fights now and it's all about that legacy," she continued. "I'm undisputed at welterweight but I can move up.
"I just want to stay on this journey with these fans."

items.title: Premier League news: Moyes demands more from Grealish, Iraola wary of United threat
items.summary: - 1. Moyes: ‘I want Jack to show more’ David Moyes has said he wants Jack Grealish to produce more for Everton as he prepares to reintegrate the playmaker into the squad. Grealish has missed Everton’s past four games mainly for disciplinary reasons having failed to report for training before last mo
items.text:
- 1. Moyes: ‘I want Jack to show more’ David Moyes has said he wants Jack Grealish to produce more for Everton as he prepares to reintegrate the playmaker into the squad. Grealish has missed Everton’s past four games mainly for disciplinary reasons having failed to report for training before last month’s Carabao Cup win over Newcastle. His last appearance for the team was in the 2-0 loss to Chelsea on 17 October but he is fit and available for Monday’s visit to Brentford. “He has served his punishment and we will treat him as we were treating him before,” the Everton manager said. “We will get on with things. The team is doing really well at the moment and what I don’t want to do is turn it into a Jack story because it shouldn’t be.” The 31-year-old played in a behind-closed-doors fixture against Derby last week andalso apologised on social media for being unable to help the team, who won three of four matches in his absence. Grealish, however, had struggled to replicate last season’s form impact when joining on loan from Manchester City prior to his breach of discipline. And Moyes is demanding more. He added: “Jack can offer us a lot. I want more from him, I want him to show more than he has done. I want him to give me more assists, more goals. There’s lots of things about him which we need and he’s good at retaining the ball, giving us good possession, carrying. So we hope that he can get back to those levels and give us what we need. I think this time last year he was probably sitting on five or six assists so we’re hoping to get that again.” The Everton manager has backed Jordan Pickford to respond strongly to the threat from James Trafford to his England place, following after the Leeds goalkeeper’s inclusion and impressive display in the Nations League win over Spain. “I don’t think it will have a great effect on him,” claimed Moyes. “If you’re playing for England you will always have other players chasing you. I still think Jordan Pickford is out there on his own at the moment. If anything, he’s getting better. It will be good for us now that he’s getting competition [with England].” Andy Hunter
- 2. United better than place in table, says Iraola Andoni Iraola has said Liverpool must disregard the latest turmoil at Manchester United and treat Sunday’s visitors like the team that thrived under Michael Carrick last season. Sunday will be the first time since March 1937 that United have faced Liverpool in a league game at Anfield while languishing in the relegation zone. Mauricio Pochettino could start his United reign bottom of the table should results on Saturday go against his new club. Iraola never lost in six league meetings with United as Bournemouth head coach. Before his first taste of the fixture with Liverpool, he insisted his north-west rivals are in a false position. “United finished third in the table last season. You are looking at a squad with exactly the same players. They had very, very good results, especially in the second half of the season,” Iraola said. “Now we have just started, it is just 10 games. For sure, they will be a lot higher in the table [soon]. We have to rate them like this and the truth is the reference we have is that they finished third. “We have to look at ourselves because we need the points. We need to improve our home form. It is also a big game in terms of relevance. It’s Liverpool v Manchester United, this is the biggest one in English football, so we want to play well and we want to win.” Iraola was boosted this week by the returns of Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni to training after serious knee injuries, although the two defenders are not yet ready for consideration. “We think they will have two weeks on and off with the group,” he said. “Then it is going to be a matter of whether we organise something behind closed doors, 11 v 11, or they straight away play with the under-21s. Before they start playing with us they have to go through that.” Liverpool’s other long-term absentee, Hugo Ekitiké, remains on course to return in January from an achilles injury. Andy Hunter
- 3. Alonso concerned by growing injury list Xabi Alonso has admitted Chelsea’s injury list is a concern. The club have a lighter schedule after their failure to qualify for Europe but they are struggling to keep players fit and have a host of selection issues before Saturday’s home game against Leeds. The Brazil striker João Pedro is yet to return from a thigh injury, Reece James is unlikely to recover from knee surgery until the new year and the France centre-back Maxence Lacroix is out with a long-term hamstring injury. Alonso is having to adjust. Jorrel Hato is unavailable in defence with a back injury and the England Under-21 winger Jamie Gittens, who has made five league starts for Chelsea since joining for £51.5m in the summer of 2025, has been out since September. “It’s a concern,” Alonso said of the injuries. “Sometimes you can analyse them and find a reason but sometimes it is difficult to find a reason.” Alonso has made 24 changes to his lineup in his first 10 league games. “It depends on the context and adaptability. I adapt to the circumstances. With the injuries you don’t have a choice. Once you have the whole menu, you can select what you like and I know what I like from the menu.” Chelsea have failed to score in three of the four league games João Pedro has missed this season. They have also had to monitor Moisés Caicedo closely, with the midfielder minding a muscle issue. But Alonso wants his side to become less reliant on Caicedo and João Pedro. “We want to have a complete squad,” he said. “That’s the goal of any manager. We have built a good squad. We are a better team with them. But it’s not about making a big drama when someone is out.” Jacob Steinberg

Sky Germany report Bayern sporting director Max Eberl confirmed shortly after the 1-1 draw that Kane had suffered a "syndesmosis ligament tear" - also known as a high ankle sprain.
The Ballon d'Or winner - who became England's most-capped player last week - was seeking a first goal in five matches for the Bundesliga leaders.
- How Bayern Munich fell in love with Harry Kane
- Kane becomes first Englishman to win Ballon d'Or for 25 years
- 'A cinderella story': Kane's journey from EFL loans to Ballon d'Or
However, as he looked to latch on to Michael Olise's deflected low cross at the back post, Cologne full-back Joel Schmied got to the ball first and clattered into Kane's left leg in his follow through.
Kane immediately clutched his lower leg and writhed in pain for a few moments before gingerly getting back to his feet, but he was a virtual bystander for the next couple of minutes.
The 33-year-old gestured to the dugout, sunk to the turf and then received treatment on his ankle before making way for Tom Bischof, limping off the field alongside two physios.
Kane had a quick exchange with Vincent Kompany, who was back in the Bayern hot-seat for the first time in six matches after being diagnosed with meningeal irritation last month, before heading down the tunnel.
To make matters worse for Bayern, Olise was also taken off injured at half-time.
How many games will Kane miss?
A three-month period on the sidelines would rule Kane out for 11 Bundesliga games, the DFB-Pokal round of 16 tie against Hertha Berlin, as well as all four of Bayern's remaining Champions League league phase matches.
Providing his recovery goes to plan, that would give the striker just over a month to prepare for England's Nations League quarter-final.
The Three Lions face Norway in Oslo in the first leg on March 27, before the return leg at Wembley on March 30.

items.title: Lampard calls for fairness after Coventry penalty row
items.summary:
Lampard calls for fairness after Coventry penalty row
- Published
Frustrated Frank Lampard has called for fairness from officials after Coventry were denied a clear penalty - with the boss claiming it got less coverage because they are a smaller club.
The Sky Blues were furious they were not awarded
items.text:
Lampard calls for fairness after Coventry penalty row
- Published
Frustrated Frank Lampard has called for fairness from officials after Coventry were denied a clear penalty - with the boss claiming it got less coverage because they are a smaller club.
The Sky Blues were furious they were not awarded a first-half spot kick in the 3-1 defeat at Everton before the international break.
James Tarkowski pulled Caleb Yirenkyi's hair in the area but was not penalised by referee Stuart Attwell or video assistant referee (VAR) Timothy Wood.
The Key Match Incidents Panel, which assesses the contentious incidents and whether the officials got them correct, this week voted unanimously that the Sky Blues should have been awarded a penalty.
It would have given Coventry a chance to go 1-0 up, before Yann Gboho fired them ahead early in the second half - only for Everton to recover.
Thierno Barry scored twice, and Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall added the third for the hosts but Lampard also argued because the decisions went against Coventry they were not given the same scrutiny as others.
"I'm not sure how much coverage it got in the days after, maybe because we're Coventry, move on everybody," said Lampard, with defeat leaving them 17th in the Premier League.
"We lost a game and we move on but we need fairness.
"If the decision is rightly for us give it to us, I'm not asking for anything beyond that.
"We're not asking for anything beyond fairness to get the right decision, to spend enough time on the decision. We're fighting on so many levels here as a promoted club.
"We've been out of the league for 25 years, we've got a lack of experience in the squad because the boys that have come up haven't played in the Premier League.
"Financially what we do in the league, in terms of where we are and the wages, we know we're right at the bottom and all these things, so we're fighting for every moment and we're grafting a lot and you just really do want that fairness."
Coventry also felt they could have had a penalty when Taiwo Awoniyi was tripped by Vitalii Mykolenko early in the second half and that Everton striker Thierno Barry handled the ball before scoring his crucial second goal.
Pro Ref chief executive Howard Webb has spoken with Lampard and Coventry sporting director Dean Austin over the decisions, with Webb acknowledging the wrong decision over the hair pull.
The hair pulling guidance was relaxed in the summer with referees advised it would not necessarily mean a straight red card, although sources accept the softening of guidance could lead to more grey areas at times - something Lampard disputed in this instance.
"There was no grey area with this, they missed it. They watched the video and they missed it," said Lampard, before Saturday's visit of Crystal Palace.
"They watched it for a good minute and a half. I've seen it and I've heard the footage. They missed it completely.
"I got fined once for talking about a referee as manager of Everton and I hate talking about it but when you work for the club you feel the pain yourself.
"You fight all week for a result and there's something with real clarity that can't really be missed. The Tarkowski one, it can't be missed at this level.
"So that's quite hard to take as well because we all saw it on the Sky broadcast pretty much straight away. So I respect and appreciate Howard Webb saying that to myself and Dean in a meeting afterwards.
"I like that side of things. Howard Webb was, when I was playing, one of the best referees in the world and I think he's very good at his job. He was upfront about the fact they missed it."

items.text:
Josh Hazlewood defends Pat Cummins over 'Sandpapergate' and backs Australia's Test captain to continue after "pile-on"
Australia captain Pat Cummins has been scrutinised after Cameron Bancroft's damning account of the 2018 sandpaper scandal; Josh Hazlewood defended Cummins in a new interview and questioned how the Test team would react if he was forced to step away as captain
Friday 20 November 2026 22:10, UK
Josh Hazlewood has defended Pat Cummins over a “pile-on” around Sandpapergate and refused to rule out boycotting the Test team if he is made to step down as captain.
Hazlewood became the latest player to break their silence over his involvement in the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, which has dominated headlines again since comments from Australian team-mate Usman Khawaja in his new autobiography 'Sabr' claimed the whole team were aware of using sandpaper.
Cameron Bancroft plunged Australian cricket into further turmoil with a 4,000-word statement, backing claims "the whole team" knew about the plot and contradicting strong denials Cummins offered in his press conference a few days earlier.
- Pat Cummins faces fresh scrutiny over Sandpapergate claims
- Sandpapergate LIVE! Latest reaction to ball-tampering scandal
- Get the latest Sky Sports deals or stream with no contract
Cummins had branded Khawaja's testimony "complete and utter nonsense" and "100 per cent wrong", leading Bancroft to go public with his story, while Australia's Test captain has had his future speculated after how he has handled the incident.
"It feels like it's been a bit of a pile on the last few days [at Cummins] from different people," Hazlewood told CodeSports. "I want to back Pat [Cummins] and everything he said in his press conference last week, everything he's done for the last five or six years in particular as captain.
"To get the group where it is now and in a position where something like that [sandpaper] is never going to happen again - I think is just a remarkable job. He's a great leader. If you went around and asked everyone in the team, you'd hear the same response.
"If we turned up for the first Test and he wasn't the captain and it was someone else, honestly, I don't know how that would go."
Australia are next in Test action when they face New Zealand in a four-match series, beginning on December 9 in Perth, where Hazlewood would consider whether to feature if Cummins was no longer captain.
"I'd have to be put in that position to make a decision, but you'd have to think about it, yeah," Hazlewood added.

Tottenham Hotspur winger Mudryk, w
items.text:
Shevchenko lying about drugs test claims - Mudryk
- Published
Mykhailo Mudryk has accused Ukraine legend Andriy Shevchenko of lying about the circumstances surrounding the winger's positive drugs test as his dispute with the country's football federation continues.
Tottenham Hotspur winger Mudryk, who is on a season-long loan from Chelsea, was suspended from November 2024 to July 2026 after testing positive for the banned substance meldonium.
In an interview on Wednesday, Mudryk said he blames the Ukrainian Association of Football (UAF) for his failed drugs test and subsequent ban, believing it entered his system while on international duty.
In response, Shevchenko, the UAF president, accused Mudryk's representatives of repeatedly asking for a UAF employee to "falsely" take the blame for his failed test.
Former Chelsea and AC Milan striker Shevchenko also said Mudryk's comments amounted to a "baseless slander against our people, who do their work honestly and professionally", and called on the player to retract his words.
In a statement on Friday, Mudryk refuted Shevchenko's accusation, saying it was a "lie" and that "neither I nor my representatives made any such request".
Mudryk has also accused the UAF of attempting to mislead his team's investigation into the reasons behind his failed test, and claims to have evidence proving it.
"My team and I repeatedly asked the UAF to help establish how I might have been exposed to meldonium and who, if anyone, might have been responsible," said Mudryk.
"In several letters to the UAF at the time, my lawyers made clear that we were seeking truthful information that could be independently verified. One of those letters was leaked to the media by the UAF earlier today and clearly shows that my lawyers wanted 'true, verifiable and reliable information'.
"Further, the UAF were repeatedly unhelpful and even attempted to mislead my team in order to distance themselves from the case. For example, UAF staff testified at my hearing that I was not using the UAF's supplements and Mr Shevchenko has repeated that assertion in his statement - but I have WhatsApp messages that prove that I was using their products during their training camps. That is, I have evidence to prove that their repeated assertions are wrong."
Mudryk also said the UAF was "repeatedly slow" to respond to requests from his team and "withheld important information and documents" from his lawyers.
BBC Sport has contacted the UAF for comment.

items.title: Ronaldo edges closer to 1,000 goals but misses penalty in Al Nassr loss
items.summary:
Cristiano Ronaldo edged closer to his 1,000th career goal and missed a first-half penalty as Al Nassr slipped to a 3-1 defeat at Saudi Pro League rivals Al Ahli.
Ronaldo fired Al Nassr in front in the 15th minute, volleying into the far corner from João Félix's assist to register his 986th goal in t
items.text:
Cristiano Ronaldo edged closer to his 1,000th career goal and missed a first-half penalty as Al Nassr slipped to a 3-1 defeat at Saudi Pro League rivals Al Ahli.
Ronaldo fired Al Nassr in front in the 15th minute, volleying into the far corner from João Félix's assist to register his 986th goal in total and his 10th of the season in all competitions for his club.
- CF7: Portugal move on from Ronaldo with 'special' goal from new No. 7 Forbs
The 41-year-old missed the chance to add to his tally four minutes later when his penalty struck a post after Nawaf Al-Boushail had been brought down in the box.
Ronaldo has now missed both of his penalty attempts for Al Nassr this season, the first time he has failed to score with consecutive penalties in the competition.
Brazilian midfielder Galeno equalized for Al Ahli on the stroke of halftime with a superb effort from outside the penalty area.
Al Ahli went ahead in the second period through Ivan Toney's penalty -- the England striker's 14th goal of the season -- and Brazil defender Roger Ibañez extended the home side's lead four minutes later.
Al Nassr remain third in the table after their second league defeat of the season, while Al Ahli's win lifts them up to fourth, four points behind Ronaldo's side.
Ronaldo's total of 986 includes a disputed goal scored on Oct. 23 against Al Faisaly, which was awarded to the Portuguese forward by the Saudi Pro League but was declared an own goal by stats provider Opta.
The record-holder for men's international appearances and goals, Ronaldo retired from playing for Portugal earlier this month.
Information from PA contributed to this report.

items.title: Sources: Tom Brady buys shares in Chelsea after Birmingham exit
items.summary:

Defense
items.text:
Seven-time Super Bowl champion quarterback Tom Brady has bought shares in Chelsea soccer club, sources confirmed to ESPN and NFL Network.
The NFL legend left the ownership group of second-tier English club Birmingham City earlier this month after becoming a minority owner with a 3.3% stake.
Defense attorney Alex Spiro is part of Brady's ownership group and helped negotiate the deal.
Brady had also held a position on the club's advisory board via a partnership with Birmingham's owner, Knighthead Capital Management, headed by his friend and business partner Tom Wagner.
Todd Boehly and fellow co-owner Mark Walter sold their stakes in Chelsea this past September in a deal that gives Clearlake Capital full control of the English Premier League club.
Private equity firm Clearlake, led by Behdad Eghbali and Jose E. Feliciano, previously owned a 61.5% stake in Chelsea, while U.S. businessmen Walter and Boehly each owned 12.83%. Swiss philanthropist Hansjörg Wyss, who also owned a 12.83% stake, remains a partner in the ownership group.
The consortium bought Chelsea for £2.5 billion ($3.3 billion) in 2022 with a further £1.75 billion ($2.3 billion) committed to investment in the club after former owner Roman Abramovich was sanctioned because of alleged ties to Russia President Vladimir Putin following the country's invasion of Ukraine.
The Financial Times reported that Walter and Boehly will receive £950 million ($1.3 billion) for their combined stake in a deal that values the club at £5 billion ($6.7 billion) including debt.
Neither Chelsea nor Clearlake Capital has replied to ESPN's request for comment about Brady's purchase of shares.
Brady purchased a 5% minority stake in the Las Vegas Raiders in 2024 after NFL owners unanimously approved the deal.
ESPN's Adam Schefter and James Olley as well as NFL Network's Ian Rapoport contributed to this report.

items.title: Pochettino: 'Massive' pressure with USMNT makes me better coach for Man United
items.summary:
Pressure? What pressure?
Mauricio Pochettino said the experience of coaching the United States at the World Cup stands him in good stead for taking over Manchester United and trying to resurrect one of soccer's fallen giants.
Pochettino left his role with the U.S. this week to take over a United tha
items.text:
Pressure? What pressure?
Mauricio Pochettino said the experience of coaching the United States at the World Cup stands him in good stead for taking over Manchester United and trying to resurrect one of soccer's fallen giants.
Pochettino left his role with the U.S. this week to take over a United that has not won the Premier League in 13 years and sits in the relegation zone after its worst start in 40 years.
- Pochettino wants input on Man United transfer decisions
- Ex-U.S. coach Arena: Federation doesn't 'have a clue' how to replace Poch
- Pochettino's Man United squad audit: Big calls to make on stars like Fernandes, Rashford
On Friday, he said his time in America means he arrives at Old Trafford at the height of his powers.
"We are much better coaches now after work in the national team like USA because the expectation and the pressure was massive," the Argentine said. "I remember in SoFi [Stadium in California], our first [World Cup] game against Paraguay, the pressure was massive. There was more than 200 celebrity people expecting us to win and to play well and all the country was behind us.
"When you are in the Premier League or in LaLiga or in France, OK, you feel the pressure when you manage these types of clubs, but being there, I promise, was massive pressure."
Pochettino teared up when he farewelled the U.S. program but on Friday he looked in his element at his first news conference in Manchester after two days working with the team.
The former Tottenham, Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea manager said he'd missed the day-to-day rhythm of club soccer.
"We were missing a lot," he said.
"I think we are animals of the grass. We like to feel the grass. We need to smell the grass and try to help the players to improve every day. It's true that it's a different job when you are in the national team, but in the same time you learn a lot and I think we are much better coaches now."
Pochettino takes over a club in crisis, on a run of one win in 10 games. United was 18th in the standings and things could get worse with a daunting trip to Liverpool on Sunday.
"It's a race to arrive in condition to be competitive against Liverpool," Pochettino said. "We arrived with the idea to create something from scratch, from our own ideas and philosophy in the way that we love to work.
"What we need to do is to be very open-minded ... the players need to buy the idea of what we need to improve. After a few days working the job is to try to find a way from Sunday to perform and to start to get the results that the club historically needs.
"Manchester United need to be in a different place than we are now."
Pochettino led the U.S. men's national team to an 8-0 aggregate win over Haiti in the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals earlier this week in the final act of his two-year stint as coach.
While U.S. Soccer looks for a permanent replacement for Pochettino, U.S. U23 coach Steve Cherundolo will lead the senior team for its December camp, which will entail a friendly with Jamaica on Dec. 13.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.

items.text:
Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane was forced off with an apparent injury to his left leg in the first half of Bayern Munich's Bundesliga clash at home to FC Cologne on Friday.
The England striker was hurt while attempting to get on the end of a deflected Michael Olise cross in front of goal, when Cologne defender Joel Schmied got to the ball first and clattered into Kane's left leg in his follow through.
Kane immediately clutched his lower leg and writhed in pain for a few moments before gingerly getting back to his feet, but he was a virtual bystander for the next couple of minutes.
The 33-year-old gestured to the dugout, sunk to the turf and then received treatment on his ankle before making way for Tom Bischof in the 20th minute, limping off the field alongside two physios.
Cologne were leading 1-0 at the time through a 12th-minute goal from Mikey Moore before Nathaniel Brown equalized in the 37th minute.
The game was Bayern's first since the November international break, in which Kane scored in England's Nations League wins over Spain and Croatia.
Bayern, who had Vincent Kompany back on the sidelines after illness, began the game level on points with Borussia Dortmund at the top of the Bundesliga.
PA contributed to this report.

items.title: Whitecaps' Müller: No relegation means MLS playing style more 'careless'
items.summary:
Vancouver Whitecaps star Thomas Müller has said that because MLS does not have a promotion/relegation system, the players feel less pressure and the playing style is more "careless, defensively."
Müller, 37, who joined the Whitecaps in August 2025 and renewed his deal through next year, is the most
items.text:
Vancouver Whitecaps star Thomas Müller has said that because MLS does not have a promotion/relegation system, the players feel less pressure and the playing style is more "careless, defensively."
Müller, 37, who joined the Whitecaps in August 2025 and renewed his deal through next year, is the most decorated German player of all time. In his 17-year career with Bayern Munich, he won a record 13 Bundesliga titles, six DFB-Pokals, eight Supercups, two Champions Leagues, two UEFA Super Cups, and two FIFA Club World Cups.
When asked to compare MLS to the Premier League or other European Leagues, the 2014 World Cup winner said MLS playing style suffers without promotion and relegation.
"It's difficult to compare because of the system," he told Canadian media outlet Global News. "There is no relegation. There is no big pressure."
He said the lack of pressure means that players lack the attention "to be focused over 90 minutes."
"[In Europe with relegation] The players have maybe no contracts for next year when you go down, so the playing style changes," he said. "When you play a bottom of the league team in Europe they fight for their lives. And sometimes I have the feeling, because of the [MLS] system, the playing style is a little bit more, let's say, optimistic, or careless, defensively.
"So a little bit, just a little bit more, the French would say, laissez faire," he said. "That's maybe good for seeing some nice offensive plays when the games are opening up. When I compare it I see sometimes really, really good individual actions in players.
"What I miss sometimes is maybe the consistency, the good and the bad, the gap is bigger.
"But the good is, we can compare it with golf, you know, even a 10-handicapper has sometimes shots a professional couldn't do better. So it's maybe the free kick, top corner free kick. But the bad shots of a professional would be never that bad. And that's a little bit, sometimes it's more like the attention of the players to be focused over 90 minutes, that's what I see sometimes, they're lacking."
Müller, who helped the Whitecaps into the MLS Cup for the first time in the club's history in 2025, only to be beaten by Inter Miami CF and Lionel Messi, said the fear of relegation helps keep teams sharp.
"[In MLS] There is, oh yeah, we do a rebuild," he said. "Nobody is happy to lose but it's totally different when you fight for getting relegated. Maybe yeah, you lose budget for the next year, the whole club. You lose people working at the club when the budget changes. It's totally different for fans."

items.title: KC Current 'peaking' at right time for NWSL Championship after past failure
items.summary:
WASHINGTON -- One year after the Kansas City Current's historic regular season was cut short in the playoffs, the team finds itself in Saturday's NWSL Championship at Audi Field against the Washington Spirit.
This year's Current was not nearly as dominant as last year's squad, but Kansas City defend
items.text:
WASHINGTON -- One year after the Kansas City Current's historic regular season was cut short in the playoffs, the team finds itself in Saturday's NWSL Championship at Audi Field against the Washington Spirit.
This year's Current was not nearly as dominant as last year's squad, but Kansas City defender Kayla Sharples said the team is better positioned to win a postseason title for the first time.
"Speaking about peaking, I do think it's different but in a better way for this season, because last year we didn't have a lot of adversity," Sharples told reporters on Friday in the press room at Audi Field.
"Winning also helps. Winning consistently masks a lot of things, so this year, we went through those ups and downs and I think that it taught us a lot about resiliency and grit, and how important that is and vital it is in order to be successful at the end of the season.
"So, because of going through that journey this season, I do believe we are peaking at the right time and that almost carries more weight than last season."
Kansas City has won seven straight games entering Saturday's final, including their quarterfinal and semifinal.
Last year's Kansas City Current team was arguably the best in NWSL history, setting several records including most points and most wins in a season while clinching the NWSL Shield earlier than any other team. But that Kansas City team, with two-time league MVP Temwa Chawinga sidelined by an injury, lost in the quarterfinals of the playoffs.
On Saturday, the Current return to Audi Field, where they lost to the Portland Thorns in the 2022 NWSL Championship, their only other appearance in the final. This time, they will face a partisan crowd in Washington's favor.
Kansas City's 2026 campaign started in turmoil for a team with explicit ambitions of being the world's best.
Chris Armas was hired as head coach in the offseason, replacing fan favorite and highly successful Vlatko Andonovski, who shifted exclusively to the sporting director role before leaving the club in September.
Multiple Kansas City starters were recovering from injuries at the beginning of the season, including Chawinga and forward Michelle Cooper.
The Current lost three straight matches in March followed by a 4-0 loss to the Spirit at Audi Field in April that left Kansas City in 14th place after Week 5 of the season.
Armas said after that third straight loss in March that the team was "building a house in a hurricane."
On Friday, ahead of the NWSL Championship match in his first year in charge, Armas said that there was "a lot of adversity and a lot of joy" through that storm.
"It was a stretch of months long of just trying to get the motor going, and it would stall a little bit and get it going, but we were building all along," Armas told reporters. "And teams do go through the phases. You either perform, and then the storm, and then you normalize. You would like to be at your best when it matters most and we think that we are probably at that moment, which means we have a chance."
Included in the Current's seven-game winning streak was a 2-1 win over the Spirit in Kansas City in October.
Armas said he remembers a 3-0 win over the Denver Summit on July 3 in Colorado, and how loud and celebratory the team bus was afterward. That stood out to him as a potential turning point, although he rejected the notion that there was a single inflection point in the season.
"I think if you asked everyone, I'm not sure we'd all have the same answer," Armas said. "I don't think it was one actual moment. The whole season has just been this process. And it oftentimes is, but it has been a story that we've been talking about, that we are the authors of. We have so much in our control."

Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk is out of contract in the summer and told Sky Sports he has "no idea" where he will be playing next season; Watch Liverpool vs Man Utd live on Sky Sports Premier League on Sunday from 4pm; kick-off 4.30pm.
Friday 20 November 2026 20:53, UK
Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk believes he can keeping playing for "many more years" - but says he does not yet know whether that will be at Anfield next season.
The 35-year-old centre-back, who has won two Premier League titles and the Champions League during his time at Liverpool, is out of contract in the summer.
He told Sky Sports that, currently, he is uncertain on what will happen beyond this campaign.
"The main thing for me is that I feel good and I'm looking after myself and I still have many more years in my opinion," he said.
"Whatever's going to happen after this season, we'll see.
